ακηδεστοσ.g: [ἀκηδεσ-, ἀκηδής.] Without funeral rites: ἐξαπολοίατʼ ἀκήδεστοι Il. 6.60.

ακηδησ.g: -ές [ἀ-1 + κῆδος.] 1 Paying no funeral rites Il. 21.123. 2 Not honoured with such rites Il. 24.554: Od. 24.187. 3 Careless, neglectful Od. 17.319. 4 Neglected Od. 6.26, Od. 19.18, Od. 20.130. 5 Vexed by no cares Il. 24.526.

ακηλητοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κηλέω, to bewitch. Cf. κηληθμός.] Proof against sorcery: νόος Od. 10.329.

ακην.g: [adv. fr. acc. of *ἀκή, silence.] 1 In silence, without speech: ἴσαν Il. 4.429. 2 Silent: ἔσαν Od. 2.82, Od. 4.285, ἔμεναι Od. 21.239 = 385. With σιωπῇ: ἀ. ἐγένοντο σιωπῇ Il. 3.95 = Il. 7.92 = 398 = Il. 8.28 = Il. 9.29 = 430 = 693 = Il. 10.218 = 313 = Il. 23.676: = Od. 8.234 = Od. 11.333 = Od. 13.1 = Od. 16.393 = Od. 20.320, Od. 7.154.

ακηρασιοσ.g: [= ἀκήρατος.] Of wine, pure, unmixed Od. 9.205 (app. by confusion with ἄκρητος).

ακηρατοσ.g: [app. = ἀκήριος1.] 1 Unharmed, intact Il. 15.498: Od. 17.532. 2 Pure, undefiled: ὕδωρ Il. 24.303 (cf. ἀκηράσιος.).

ακηριοσ2.g: [ἀ-1 + κῆρ.] 1 Lifeless: βέλος ἀκήριον τίθησιν Il. 11.392. Cf. Il. 21.466. 2 Spiritless: δέος Il. 5.812, 817, Il. 13.224, ἥμενοι ἀκήριοι Il. 7.100.

ακιδνοσ.g: In comp. ἀκιδνότερος, -η App., of less account, less to be regarded Od. 5.217, Od. 8.169, Od. 18.130.

ακικυσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κῖκυς.] Without strength, feeble: ὀλίγος (κακὸς) καὶ ἀ. Od. 9.515, Od. 21.131.

ακιχητοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κιχάνω.] Not to be reached. Absol. in neut. pl. ἀκίχητα, the unattainable Il. 17.75.

ακλαυτοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κλαυ-, κλαίω.] 1 Unwept: νέκυς Il. 22.386. Cf. Od. 11.54, 72. 2 Not weeping Od. 4.494.

ακλεησ.g: [ἀ-1 + κλέος.] Acc. ἀκλέα (for ἀκλεέα) Od. 4.728. Nom. pl. ἀκλεέες Il. 12.318. 1 Without fame, inglorious Il. 12.318. In neut. ἀκλεές as adv. = ἀκλειῶς 1: ἥμενοι Il. 7.100. 2 (So as to be) the subject of no tidings: παῖδʼ ἀνηρείψαντο θύελλαι ἀκλέα Od. 4.728.

ακλειωσ.g: [adv. fr. ἀκλεής. Doubtless for ἀκλεεῶς.] 1 In inglorious wise: μὴ ἀ. ἀπολοίμην Il. 22.304. 2 So that no tidings come: ἀ. μιν ἅρπυιαι ἀνηρείψαντο Od. 1.241 = Od. 14.371.

ακληροσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κλῆρος.] Having no (considerable) portion of land: ἀνδρί Od. 11.490.

ακμηνοσ.g:
Fasting Il. 19.207, 346. Not partaking of (food or drink). With genit.: σίτοιο Il. 19.163, πόσιος καὶ ἐδητύος 320.
[ἀκμή in sense highest point.] In its prime, flourishing: θάμνος ἐλαίης Od. 23.191.

ακμησ.g: -ῆτος [ἀ-1 + κ(α)μ-, κάμνω.] 1 Not tired, fresh Il. 11.802 = Il. 16.44. 2 Tireless Il. 15.697.

ακμοθετον.g: -ου, τό [ἄκμων + θε-, τίθημι.] An anvil-block Il. 18.410, 476: Od. 8.274.

ακνηστισ.g: ἡ [prob. conn. with ἄκανθα in sense spine, prickle.] The backbone or spine Od. 10.161.

ακοιτησ.g: -ου, ὁ [ἀ-2 + κοῖτος.] A husband, one's husband Il. 15.91: Od. 5.120, Od. 21.88.

ακομιστιη.g: -ης, ἡ [ἀ-1 + κομίζω.] Lack of tendance or care: ἄλη τʼ ἀκομιστίη τε Od. 21.284.

ακοντιζω.g: [ἄκων.] 3 sing. aor. ἀκόντισε Il. 4.496, Il. 5.533, Il. 8.118, Il. 13.183, Il. 17.304, etc. 3 pl. ἠκόντισαν Il. 16.336. ἀκόντισαν Il. 22.255, 265, 272, 282. Imp. pl. ἀκοντίσατε Od. 22.252. Genit. sing. masc. pple. ἀκοντίσσαντος Il. 4.498, Il. 15.575. Infin. ἀκοντίσσαι Il. 13.559, 585, Il. 16.359. ἀκοντίσαι Od. 22.263. (ἀν-.) 1 To throw the spear: ἀνδρὸς ἀκοντίσσαντος Il. 4.498 = Il. 15.575. Cf. Il. 16.336, 359: οἱ ἓξ ἀκοντίσατε Od. 22.252. Cf. Od. 22.255, 263. With genit. of the person aimed at: Ἕκτορος ἀκόντισεν Il. 8.118. Cf. Il. 13.502, 559, Il. 17.608. With dat. of the weapon: δουρί Il. 5.533. Cf. Il. 4.496, Il. 5.611 = Il. 17.347, Il. 11.577, Il. 13.403, 585, Il. 15.573, Il. 16.284, Il. 17.574: Od. 8.229. With genit and dat. Il. 4.490, Il. 13.183, 516, Il. 14.402, 461, Il. 15.429, Il. 17.304, 525. 2 To throw (a spear): αἰχμάς Il. 12.44, Il. 14.422: δοῦρα Od. 22.265, 272, 282.

ακοντιστησ.g: -οῦ, ὁ [ἀκοντίζω.] A (skilful) spearman: υἷες ἀκοντισταὶ Ἀμισωδάρου Il. 16.328. Cf. Od. 18.262.

ακοντιστυσ.g: ἡ [as ἀκοντιστής.] A contest of throwing the spear: οὐδʼ ἔτʼ ἀκοντιστὺν ἐσδύσεαι Il. 23.622.

ακορητοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κόρος.] Insatiable in, never having his or their fill of. With genit.: μόθου Il. 7.117. Cf. Il. 12.335, Il. 13.621, 639, Il. 14.479, Il. 20.2.

ακοσ.g: τό. A cure or remedy Il. 9.250: Od. 22.481.

ακοσμοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κόσμος.] Disorderly, marked by turbulence: ἔπεα Il. 2.213.

ακοστεω.g: [ἀκοστή, cited as barley.] To have barley for food, be corn-fed: ἀκοστήσας ἐπὶ φάτνῃ Il. 6.506 = Il. 15.263.

ακουαζομαι.g: [ἀκούω.] To listen to, give ear to. With genit.: ἀοιδοῦ Od. 9.7, Od. 13.9. To hear of. With double genit. of person from whom one hears of a thing and of the thing: δαιτὸς ἐμεῖο Il. 4.343.

ακουη.g: -ῆς, ἡ [ἀκούω.] 1 A sound Od. 16.634. 2 News, tidings Od. 2.308, Od. 4.701 = Od. 5.19, Od. 14.179, Od. 17.43.

ακουω.g: Dat. pl. masc. pres. pple. ἀκουόντεσσι Od. 1.352. 2 sing. fut. in mid. form ἀκούσεαι Il. 15.96. 3 pl. ἀκούσονται Il. 15.199. Aor. ἤκουσα -ας Il. 1.381, Il. 16.531, Il. 22.447: Od. 11.421, Od. 12.265, 389, Od. 17.492, Od. 19.89, Od. 22.354, 361. ἄκουσα, -ας Il. 1.396, Il. 2.16, 194, Il. 6.166, Il. 7.53, Il. 10.276, Il. 17.256, Il. 21.98, Il. 24.223, etc.: Od. 2.412, 423, Od. 3.94, Od. 4.281, Od. 8.95, Od. 12.202, Od. 15.92, Od. 21.210, Od. 23.326, etc. Subj. ἀκούσω, -ῃς Il. 14.90, Il. 17.245, Il. 21.475, 575: Od. 1.94, 282, Od. 2.216, Od. 3.83, Od. 11.561, Od. 12.41, Od. 16.32, Od. 21.237, etc. 3 sing. opt. ἀκούσαι Il. 7.129, Il. 19.81. 3 pl. ἀκούσειαν Il. 2.98, 282. Imp. ἄκουσον Il. 6.334, Il. 9.262: Od. 6.325, Od. 12.37, Od. 15.318, Od. 19.535, etc. 3 sing. ἀκουσάτω Od. 16.301. Pple. ἀκούσας, -αντος Il. 3.76, Il. 4.198, Il. 8.319, Il. 10.184, Il. 17.694, etc.: Od. 4.114, Od. 8.491, Od. 10.556, Od. 15.98. Infin. ἀκοῦσαι Od. 2.375, Od. 4.553, Od. 12.187, Od. 17.115, etc. (ἐπ-, ἐσ-, ὑπ-.) 1 To hear: τέρπετʼ ἀκούων Il. 1.474. Cf. Il. 4.198, Il. 11.603, Il. 15.129, Il. 17.245, Il. 18.35, etc.: ἐθέλω ἀκοῦσαι Od. 4.553. Cf. Od. 11.380, Od. 12.48, Od. 15.98, Od. 23.135, etc. With dependent clause: ὡς ἐβόησας Od. 4.281. 2 In various constructions. a α With acc. of what is heard: μῦθον Il. 2.16. Cf. Il. 1.547, Il. 2.486, Il. 4.435, Il. 6.524, Il. 10.354, Il. 21.575, etc.: δοῦπον Od. 5.401. Cf. Od. 1.282, Od. 11.421, Od. 12.265, Od. 23.40, etc. β With this acc. and genit. of person from whom one hears: σεῦ τὸν μῦθον Il. 19.185, σεῦ κακὸν ἔπος Il. 24.767: ἄλλων μῦθον Od. 2.314. Cf. Od. 3.94 = Od. 4.324. With this acc. and prep.: ἐκ δεσποίνης ἔπος Od. 15.374. b α With acc. of what is heard about: κακὰ ἔργα Il. 9.595. Cf. Il. 15.96, Il. 18.53: πατρὸς βίοτον Od. 1.287. Cf. Od. 2.218, Od. 8.578, Od. 16.380, Od. 19.535. β With this acc. and genit. of person from whom one hears: τόδε πατρός Od. 8.564, ταῦτα καλυψοῦς Od. 12.389, [ταῦθʼ] Ἑρμείαο 390. γ With this acc. and acc. pple. expressing what is heard about a person: τοὺς εἰ πτώσσοντας ἀκούσαι Il. 7.129. δ With infin. so expressing: τείρεσθαι Τρῶας Il. 6.386. ε With prep.: Ὀδυσῆος περὶ νόστου Od. 19.270. c With genit. of what is heard: κωκυτοῦ Il. 22.447. Cf. Od. 12.265, Od. 21.237 = 383, Od. 21.290, 292. d With genit. of person heard: ὁμοκλητῆρος Il. 12.273. Cf. Il. 16.211, Il. 23.452, Il. 24.223: Od. 14.493, Od. 19.89, Od. 22.361. So in reference to a beast: θηρός Il. 10.184. e α With genit, and pple. in agreement, to hear a person doing or suffering something: ὀτρύνοντος Ἕκτορος Il. 15.506. Cf. Il. 1.396, Il. 21.475: τοῦ βλημένου Od. 17.492. Cf. Od. 9.497, Od. 10.221, Od. 21.210. β With pple. alone: στενάχοντος Od. 8.95 = 534. So in reference to a bird: κλάγξαντος Il. 10.276. f With genit. of person from whom one hears about something: ἄλλου Od. 8.491. g α With genit. of person heard about and pple. in agreement expressing what is heard: σέθεν ζώοντος Il. 24.490. Cf. Od. 11.458, Od. 16.301. β With adj.: Ὀδυσῆος ζωοῦ Od. 17.525. γ With double genit. of person from whom one hears and of person heard about and adj. in genit. joined with pple.: Ὀδυσσῆος ζωοῦ οὐδὲ θανόντος τευ ἀκοῦσαι Od. 17.115. δ With genit. of person heard about omitted: τεθνηῶτος Od. 1.289. Cf. Od. 2.220, 375, Od. 4.728, 748. ε With this genit. alone: πατρός Od. 4.114. 3 To listen, hearken, give ear: θεοὶ πάντες ἄκουον Il. 8.4. Cf. Il. 12.442, Il. 17.408, Il. 19.81: ἥατʼ ἀκούοντες Od. 1.326. Cf. Od. 1.352, 353, Od. 12.37, Od. 15.393. 4 To listen to, give ear to. a With acc. of what is listened to: ἄλλων μῦθον Il. 2.200. Cf. Il. 8.492: Od. 8.429, Od. 20.389.– b With genit. of person: βασιλήων Il. 2.98. Cf. Il. 6.334, Il. 9.262, Il. 19.79, 256: ἀοιδοῦ Od. 1.370. Cf. Od. 7.11, Od. 9.3, Od. 15.318 = Od. 24.265, Od. 16.259, Od. 17.520, Od. 18.129.– c α With genit. of person, to listen to in sense of yielding or obeying: εἰπόντος Il. 6.281. Cf. Il. 15.199: Od. 2.423, Od. 19.419, Od. 22.354. Sim., in mid., οὔ πώ σφιν ἀκούετο λαὸ

ακρααντοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κραιαίνω.] 1 Not accomplished, not carried out: ἔργον Il. 2.138. 2 Not to be fulfilled: ἔπεα Od. 19.565. In neut. ἀκράαντον as adv., without hope of fulfilment, to no purpose Od. 2.202.

ακραησ.g: [ἄκρος + ἄημι.] (Cf. ὑπεραής.) Acc. sing. ἀκραῆ Od. 2.421. Of wind, blowing at height; or perh., blowing with the right velocity or from the right quarter Od. 2.421, Od. 14.253, 299.

ακρη.g: -ης, ἡ [fem. of ἄκρος as sb..] 1 The highest point of a city Od. 8.508. 2 κατʼ ἄκρης, down from the top. Of a breaking wave, with full force Od. 5.313. Fig., utterly, to total destruction: ὤλετο Il. 13.772. Cf. Il. 15.557, Il. 22.411, Il. 24.728. 3 A cape or headland Il. 4.425, Il. 14.36: Od. 9.285.

ακρητοσ.g: -ον [ἀ-1 + κρη-, κεράννυμι.] Unmixed: οἴνῳ Od. 24.73. Cf. Od. 2.341, Od. 9.297. So σπονδαὶ ἄκρητοι (ratified by libations of unmixed wine) Il. 2.341 = Il. 4.159.

ακρισ.g:
-ίδος, ἡ. A locust Il. 21.12.
-ιος, ἡ [ἄκρος.] A hill-top: ἠνεμοέσσας Od. 9.400, Od. 16.365, διʼ ἄκριας Od. 10.281, Od. 14.2.

ακριτομυθοσ.g: [ἄκριτος + μῦθος.] 1 Indiscriminate or reckless in speech Il. 2.246. 2 Hard to be discerned or interpreted ὄνειροι Od. 19.560.

ακριτοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + κρίνω.] 1 Indiscriminate, endless: μῦθοι Il. 2.796. Endless, never-ending: ἄχεα Il. 3.412, Il. 24.91. Endless, never brought to reconciliation: νείκεα Il. 14.205 = 304. Absol. in neut. pl.: ἄκριτα πόλλʼ ἀγόρευον Od. 8.505 (app., held much and indiscriminate or inconsistent debate). 2 In neut. sing. ἄκριτον as adv. a Indiscriminately: ἐξαγαγόντες ἀ. ἐκ πεδίου (see ἐξάγω 2) Il. 7.337, 436. b Endlessly, continually: πενθήμεναι Od. 18.174, Od. 19.120.

ακριτοφυλλοσ.g: [ἄκριτος + φύλλον.] With confused or massed foliage: ὄρος Il. 2.868 (i.e. the separate trees are indistinguishable).

ακροκουοσ.g: [ἄκρος + κόμη.] Wearing the hair in a topknot (the hair round this being app. cut short or shaved off). Epithet of the Thracians Il. 4.533.

ακρον.g: -ου, τό [neut. of ἄκρος as sb..] 1 The summit or crest of a hill Od. 11.597. 2 A cape or headland. Of Sunium Od. 3.278. 3 An end or extremity: ἐπʼ ἄκρῳ δῆσε ζυγόν Il. 5.729. Cf. Od. 9.328, 382. 4 The extreme surface: [νύσσης] Il. 23.339.

ακροπολισ.g: ἡ [ἄκρος + πόλις.] The highest part of a city, the citadel. Of Troy Od. 8.494, 504.

ακροπολοσ.g: [ἄκρος. Cf. οἰόπολος.] Topmost, the topmost part of: ὄρεσσιν Il. 5.523: Od. 19.205.

ακροποροσ.g: [ἄκρος + πείρω.] With a piercing or sharp point. Epithet of spits: ὀβελούς Od. 3.463.

ακροσ.g: -η, -ον. Extreme, at the furthest point. 1 Topmost, the topmost part of: πόλει Il. 6.88 (the citadel), πρώονες Il. 8.557 = Il. 16.299. Cf. Il. 5.460, Il. 6.257, 297, 317, 512, Il. 7.345, Il. 8.83, Il. 9.241, Il. 11.351, Il. 12.282, Il. 13.523, 615, Il. 14.292, 352, Il. 15.152, Il. 22.383: σκοπέλοισιν Od. 12.239. 2 Outermost, the extremity of: πόδας Il. 16.640. Cf. Il. 17.264 (see ἠϊών 2), 309, 599, Il. 20.227: οἰήϊον Od. 9.483 = 540. The edge of: χείλει Il. 12.51. Growing on the extremity: τρίχες οὐραῖαι Il. 23.519. At the end of a row: νῆες Il. 15.653. The base or root of: χεῖρα Il. 5.336 (cf. 458). 3 The surface of: ὕδωρ Il. 16.162: ῥινόν Od. 22.278. App. in neut. ἄκρον as adv., on the surface: ἀ. ἐπὶ ῥηγμῖνος θέεσκον Il. 20.229 (v. l. ἀ. ἔπι, taking ἀ. as sb., the surface; see ἄκρον 4). 4 In superl. ἀκρότατος, -η, -ον (in Od. 12.11 of two terminations), much like the positive. a Topmost, the topmost part of: κορυφῇ Il. 1.499 = Il. 5.754 = Il. 8.3. Cf. Il. 2.793, Il. 6.470, Il. 13.12, Il. 14.157, 228, 285, Il. 15.536, Il. 20.52, Il. 22.172: τύμβῳ Od. 12.15. Absol.: ἐπʼ ἀκροράτῃ (at the top) Il. 4.484. b The extremity of: ὄζῳ Il. 2.312. Sim. ἀκρότατον παρʼ οὐδόν Od. 22.127 (app., to one side of (and passing at right angles) one of the extremities of the threshold). Predicatively: ὅθʼ ἀκρότατος πρόεχʼ ἀκτή (where the beach ran furthest out) Od. 12.11. c The surface of: χρόα Il. 4.139, χαλκόν Il. 7.246.

ακτη1,.g: -ῆς, ἡ. Corn or meal: ἀλφίτου Il. 11.631, δημήτερος Il. 13.322, Il. 21.76: ἀλφίτου Od. 2.355, Od. 14.429.

ακτη2,.g: -ῆς, ἡ. 1 A beach or shore of the sea: ἀκτὴν εἰσανέβαινον Il. 18.68. Cf. Il. 12.284, Il. 20.50, Il. 23.125, Il. 24.97: ἐπʼ ἀκτῆς καθήμενος Od. 5.82. Cf. Od. 5.151, Od. 10.140, 509, Od. 13.234, Od. 15.36, Od. 24.378. 2 A projecting part of the shore: ἀκτῇ Il. 2.395: ἀκταὶ προβλῆτες Od. 5.405. Cf. Od. 5.425, Od. 10.89, Od. 12.11, Od. 13.98, Od. 24.82.

ακτημων.g: [ἀ-1 + κτῆμα.] Not possessed of, lacking. With genit.: χρυσοῖο Il. 9.126 = 268.

ακτισ.g: ἡ. Dat. pl. ἀκτῖσι Od. 5.479, Od. 19.441. ἀκτίνεσσι Il. 10.547: Od. 11.16. A ray or beam: ἠελίοιο Il. 10.547. Cf. Od. 5.479, Od. 11.16, Od. 19.441.

ακυλοσ.g: -ου. Prob., the fruit of the ilex. Given to swine Od. 10.242.

ακων.g: -οντος, ὁ. 1 A dart or javelin Il. 4.137, Il. 10.335, Il. 11.364 = Il. 20.451, Il. 11.675, Il. 14.455, Il. 15.646, 709, Il. 16.361, Il. 20.413, 455, 486, Il. 21.590: Od. 14.225, 531, Od. 21.340. Used for guarding cattle or sheep Il. 11.552 = Il. 17.661, Il. 12.306: Od. 13.225. 2 In generalized sense, the dart: ἐπιστάμενος ἄκοντι Il. 15.282.

αλαδε.g: [acc. of ἅλς1 + -δε 1.] To or into the sea: νῆα προέρυσσεν Il. 1.308. Cf. Il. 2.165 = 181, Il. 5.598, Il. 9.358, 683, Il. 12.19, Il. 14.97, 100, 106: νῆʼ εἴρυσεν Od. 2.389. With εἰς: ποταμῶν, οἵ τʼ εἰς ἁ. προπέουσιν Od. 10.351.

αλαλητοσ.g: -οῦ, ὁ [imitative.] A shouting Il. 2.149: Od. 24.463. A shouting in distress: ἀλαλητῷ φεύγοντες Il. 18.149. Cf. Il. 21.10. A shouting in war, the war-shout: ἀ. ἀνὰ στρατὸν ὀρώρει Il. 4.436. Cf. Il. 12.138, Il. 14.393, Il. 16.78.

αλαλκομενηισ.g: [app. fr. ἄλαλκον.] Thus, the guardian or protectress. Epithet of Athene Il. 4.8, Il. 5.908.

αλαλκον.g: aor. [cf. ἀλκή, ἀλέξω.] (ἀπ-.) 1 To ward or keep off Il. 9.605, Il. 21.548, Il. 23.185: Od. 4.167. With dat. of person protected: κύνας οἱ Il. 17.153. Cf. Il. 19.30, Il. 21.138 = 250: Od. 3.237, Od. 13.319. With genit.: Τρώων λοιγόν Il. 21.539. With dat. and genit. of part: κρατός τοι κακὸν ἦμαρ Od. 10.288. 2 With dat., to succour, defend, protect: οἱ Il. 22.196.

αλαλυκτημαι.g: [pf. pass. fr. *ἀλυκτέω, conn. with ἀλύω.] To be distraught or sore distressed Il. 10.94.

αλαομαι.g: [ἄλη.] 3 pl. ἀλόωνται Od. 3.73, Od. 9.254. Imp. ἀλόω Od. 5.377. Aor. ἀλήθην Od. 14.120. 2 sing. ἀλήθης Od. 14.362. Pple. ἀληθείς Od. 14.380, Od. 16.205. Pf. ἀλάλημαι Il. 23.74: Od. 11.167. 2 sing. ἀλάλησαι Od. 15.10. 3 sing. ἀλάληται Od. 20.340. 2 pl. ἀλάλησθε Od. 3.72, Od. 9.253. Imp. ἀλάλησο Od. 3.313. Pple. ἀλαλήμενος Od. 13.333, Od. 14.122, Od. 17.245, Od. 21.327. Infin. ἀλάλησθαι Od. 2.370, Od. 12.284, Od. 15.276, Od. 20.206. (ἐπ-.) To wander, rove: κὰπ πεδίον ἀλᾶτο Il. 6.201. Cf. Il. 2.667, Il. 8.482, Il. 10.141, Il. 23.74: μαψιδίως Od. 3.72. Cf. Od. 2.333, 370, Od. 3.73, Od. 4.91, Od. 5.336, etc.

αλαοσ.g: Blind: μάντιος ἀλαοῦ (for ἀλαόο) Od. 10.493, Od. 12.267. Absol., a blind man Od. 8.195.

αλαοσκοπιη.g: -ῆς, ἡ [ἀλαός + σκοπιή. Blind watch.] A negligent or careless watch or lookout: οὐδʼ ἀλαοσκοπιὴν εἶχεν Il. 10.515, Il. 13.10, Il. 14.135: Od. 8.285.

αλαοω.g: [ἀλαός]. (ἐξ-) To blind: ὀφθαλμοῦ (of his (my) eye) Od. 1.69, Od. 9.516.

αλαπαδνοσ.g: -ή, -όν [ἀλαπάζω.] 1 Weak, feeble, ineffective: στίχες Il. 4.330, σθένος Il. 5.783 = Il. 7.257, Il. 8.463: Od. 18.373. Comp. ἀλαπαδνότερος Il. 4.305. 2 Having little power or influence Il. 2.675.

αλαπαζω.g: 2 sing. fut. ἀλαπάξεις Il. 2.367. Aor. ἀλάπαξα Il. 9.328, Il. 11.750. 3 sing. -ε Od. 17.424, Od. 19.80. Infin. ἀλαπάξαι Il. 9.136, 278. (ἐξ-.) 1 To deprive of vigour, take the strength from: Ἀχαιούς Il. 12.67. To ruin: Ζεὺς ἀλάπαξεν (brought all this to nought) Od. 17.424 = Od. 19.80. To work havoc in (opposed ranks) Il. 5.166, Il. 11.503. 2 To slay Il. 11.750. 3 To destroy or sack (a city) Il. 2.367, Il. 9.136 = 278, 328, Il. 24.245.

αλαστεω.g: [ἄλαστος.] (ἐπ-) To find things intolerable: ἠλάστεον θεοί (raged (impotently)) Il. 15.21. So in aor. pple. ἀλαστήσας, giving way to such a feeling, breaking out in protest Il. 12.163.

αλαστοσ.g: [prob. ἀ-1 + λαθ-, λανθάνω.] Thus 1 Unforgettable, that never leaves one: πένθος Il. 24.105: Od. 1.342, Od. 24.423, ἄχος Od. 4.108. In neut. ἄλαστον as adv., of mourning, without power of forgetting, unceasingly: ὀδύρομαι Od. 14.174. 2 Applied to a person (app. by transference of the epithet from acts to the agent), doer of deeds not to be forgotten, wretch: Ἕκτορ, ἄλαστε Il. 22.261.

αλγεω.g: [ἄλγος.] To suffer (bodily) pain or discomfort Il. 2.269, Il. 8.85, Il. 12.206: Od. 12.27.

αλγιον.g: [neut. comp. fr. ἄλγος.] So much the worse, all the harder: ἀ. τῷ ἔσσεται Il. 18.306. Cf. Il. 18.278: Od. 17.14, Od. 19.322. Without construction Od. 4.292, Od. 16.147.

αλγιστοσ.g: -η, -ον [superl. formed as ἄλγιον.] Most difficult or hard: ἀλγίστη δαμάσασθαι Il. 23.655.

αλγοσ.g: τό. 1 Pain, distress: ἀ. ἱκάνει θυμόν Il. 3.97. Cf. Il. 6.450, 462, Il. 18.395, Il. 22.53, 54: ὅπως μοι ἀ. ἀλάλκοις Od. 13.319. Cf. Od. 2.41, 193, Od. 15.345, Od. 19.471. 2 Definitely distinguished as bodily pain or suffering Il. 5.394: Od. 14.32. 3 In pl., distresses, woes, cares, hardships: Ἀχαιοῖς ἄλγεʼ ἔθηκεν Il. 1.2. Cf. Il. 2.667, Il. 9.321, Il. 13.346, Il. 18.224, Il. 24.568, etc.: πάθεν ἄλγεα Od. 1.4, ἄλγεσι θυμὸν ἐρέχθων Od. 5.83 (i.e. expressions of grief). Cf. Od. 2.343, Od. 3.220, Od. 8.182, Od. 20.339, etc.

αλεγεινοσ.g: -ή, -όν [ἄλγος.] 1 Causing pain or grief, painful, grievous, hard Il. 2.787, Il. 4.99, Il. 5.658, Il. 9.546, Il. 11.398, Il. 13.569, Il. 15.16, Il. 18.17, 248 = Il. 19.46 = Il. 20.43, Il. 23.653, 701: Od. 3.206, Od. 8.126, Od. 10.78, Od. 12.26, 226. 2 Causing or apt to cause injury or harm: πνοιῇ βορέω Il. 14.395. Cf. Il. 17.749, Il. 24.8: = Od. 8.183 = Od. 13.91 = 264, Od. 18.224. 3 Fatal, baneful: ἀγηνορίης Il. 22.457. 4 Difficult, troublesome: δαμήμεναι Il. 10.402, Il. 17.76. Troublesome, irksome: νηπιέῃ Il. 9.491. 5 App., bringing repentance in its wake: μαχλοσύνην Il. 24.30.

αλεγιζω.g: [cf. ἀλέγω.] With neg., not to care for, trouble oneself about, have regard for. With genit.: σέθεν οὐκ ἀλεγίζω Il. 1.180. Cf. Il. 1.160, Il. 8.477, Il. 11.80, Il. 12.238. Absol. Il. 15.106.

αλεγυνω.g: [cf. ἀλέγω.] To take one's part in, partake of (a meal): δαῖτας Od. 1.374. Cf. Od. 2.139, Od. 8.38, Od. 11.186, Od. 13.23.

αλεγω.g: 1 To care, be concerned: οὐκ ἀλέγω Il. 11.389: Od. 17.390. 2 To be careful of one's duties, show due regard for another or others: ὅτις οὐκ ἀλέγει Od. 16.307. Cf. Od. 19.154. 3 To show concern for, busy oneself with, the right: λιταὶ ἀλέγουσιν Il. 9.504. 4 To attend to, busy oneself about: νηῶν ὅπλα Od. 6.268. 5 With neg., not to care for or concern oneself about, regard or heed: θεῶν ὄπιν οὐκ ἀλέγοντες Il. 16.388. With genit.: σκυζομένης σευ Il. 8.483. Cf. Od. 9.115, 275, Od. 20.214.

αλεεινω.g: [cf. ἀλέομαι.] 1 To escape, evade, avoid, keep out of the way, reach or influence of, avoid incurring (something coming upon or threatening one): κῆρα Il. 3.32 = Il. 11.585 = Il. 13.566 = 596 = 648 = Il. 14.408, Il. 16.817. Cf. Il. 11.794, Il. 13.669, Il. 16.36, 213 = Il. 23.713, Il. 17.374: χόλον γυναικός Od. 1.433. Cf. Od. 5.326, Od. 6.273, Od. 13.148, Od. 19.373, Od. 24.229. 2 To elude the notice of Od. 16.477. Absol., to evade questioning Od. 4.251. 3 To shun, avoid, keep clear of or away from: πάτον ἀνθρώπων Il. 6.202. Cf. Il. 11.542, Il. 23.422. 4 With infin., to shrink from doing, hesitate to do: κτεῖναι Il. 6.167, ἀλεξέμεναι Il. 13.356.

αλεη1.g: ἡ [ἀλέομαι.] A means of escape Il. 22.301.

αλειτησ.g: -ου, ὁ [ἀλετεῖν, aor. infin. ἀλιταίνω.] An offender: τείσεσθαι ἀλείτην Il. 3.28. Cf. Od. 20.121.

αλειφαρ.g: -ατος, τό [ἀλείφω.] Unguent, oil Il. 18.351, Il. 23.170: Od. 3.408 (app. here some kind of polish or varnish), Od. 24.45, 67, 73.

αλεν.g:
3 pl. aor. pass. εἴλω.
neut. aor. pple. pass. εἴλω.

αλεξανεμοσ.g: -ον [ἀλέξω + ἄνεμος.] Protecting from the wind: χλαῖναν Od. 14.529.

αλεξητηρ.g: -ῆρος, ὁ [ἀλέξω.] One who wards off or stems: ἀλεξητῆρα μάχης Il. 20.396.

αλεξικακοσ.g: -ον [ἀλέξω + κακόν. See κακός 11.] Tending to avert evil: μῆτις Il. 10.20.

αλεξω.g: [cf. ἄλαλκον.] 2 sing. fut. ἀλεξήσεις Il. 9.251. Acc. sing. masc. pple. ἀλεξήσοντα Il. 6.109. Infin. ἀλεξήσειν Il. 20.315, Il. 21.374. 3 sing. aor. opt. ἀλεξήσειε Od. 3.346. Aor. infin. mid. ἀλέξασθαι Il. 13.475, Il. 15.565, Il. 16.562: Od. 18.62. (ἀπ-, ἐπ-.) 1 To ward or keep off, avert Od. 3.346. With dat. of person or thing protected: Δαναοῖσι κακὸν ἦμαρ Il. 9.251. Cf. Il. 9.347, 674, Il. 17.365, Il. 20.315 = Il. 21.374. 2 With dat., to succour, defend, protect: ἀλλήλοισιν Il. 3.9. Cf. Il. 5.779, Il. 6.109. Absol., to afford succour, defence, or protection Il. 1.590, Il. 11.469, Il. 13.356. 3 In mid., to ward or keep off from oneself, defend oneself against, encounter: ἀλέξασθαι κύνας Il. 13.475: τοῦτον ἀλέξασθαι Od. 18.62. Absol., to defend oneself, offer resistance Il. 11.348 = Il. 22.231, Il. 15.565 = Il. 16.562: Od. 9.57.

αλετρισ.g: ἡ [ἀλέω.] A female slave employed in grinding Od. 20.105.

αλεωρη.g: -ῆς, ἡ [ἀλέομαι.] 1 Shrinking from the foe Il. 24.216. 2 A means of defence: δηΐων ἀνδρῶν (against . . .) Il. 12.57, Il. 15.533.

αληθησ.g: -ές [ἀ-1 + λήθω.] 1 App., not forgetting, careful, anxious: χερνῆτις Il. 12.433. 2 Absol. in neut. pl. ἀληθέα, the truth Il. 6.382: Od. 3.254 = Od. 16.61, Od. 13.254, Od. 14.125, Od. 17.15, Od. 18.342. 3 In neut. sing. ἀληθές as adv., truly Od. 3.247.

αληιοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + ληΐς.] Without share of booty; hence, not rich in possessions Il. 9.125 = 267.

αλητευω.g: [ἀλήτης.] 1 To wander, rove Od. 12.330, Od. 14.126, Od. 16.101, Od. 18.114. 2 To go to and fro: κατὰ δῶμα Od. 17.501. Cf. Od. 22.291.

αλιαησ.g: [ἅλς1 + ἄημι.] Blowing over the sea Od. 4.361.

αλιαστοσ.g: -ον [ἀ-1 + λιάζομαι.] 1 Unabating, unceasing Il. 2.797, Il. 12.471 = Il. 16.296, Il. 14.57, Il. 20.31, Il. 24.760. 2 In neut., ἀλίαστον as adv., without ceasing Il. 24.549.

αλιγκιοσ.g: Like, resembling. With dat.: ἀστέρι καλῷ Il. 6.401: ἀθανάτοισιν Od. 8.174.

αλιευσ.g: -ῆος, ὁ [ἅλιος1.] 1 A seaman Od. 24.419. With ἐρέτης Od. 16.349. 2 A fisher Od. 12.251, Od. 22.384.

αλιμυρηεισ.g: -εντος [ἅλς1 + μύρω.] Seaward flowing Il. 21.190. Of a river at its meeting with the sea Od. 5.460.

αλιοσ2,.g: -η, -ον. 1 Ineffective, effecting nothing, useless, idle, vain, fruitless: πόνον Il. 4.26. Cf. Il. 4.158, 179, 498 = Il. 15.575, Il. 5.18, 715, Il. 11.376, 380, Il. 14.455, Il. 16.480, Il. 18.324, Il. 24.92, 224: ὁδός Od. 2.273, 318. Of a person, inefficient: σκοπός Il. 10.324. 2 In neut. ἅλιον as adv., in vain, without result Il. 13.410, 505 = Il. 16.615.

αλιοω.g: [ἅλιος 2.] 1 To make of no effect, frustrate: Διὸς νόον Od. 5.104 = 138. 2 To use to no effect: βέλος (did not hurl it in vain) Il. 16.737.

αλιπλοοσ.g: [ἅλς1 + πλέω.] Floating on the sea, in the state of flotsam: τείχεα Il. 12.26.

αλιπορφυροσ.g: [ἅλς1 + (app.) πορφύρα, the Phoenician shell-fish called the murex, the dye got therefrom.] Thus, dyed in sea-purple: ἠλάκατα Od. 6.53, 306, φάρεα Od. 13.108.

αλισ.g: (ϝάλις) [ἀλ-, (ϝ)είλω.] 1 In a throng, in swarms: μέλισσαι ἁ. πεποτήαται Il. 2.90. Cf. Il. 3.384, Il. 22.473. 2 In abundance, in plenty, in great numbers: ἁ. οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι Il. 14.122. Cf. Il. 9.137, 279, Il. 17.54, Il. 21.236, 319, 344, 352, Il. 22.340: χαλκὸν ἁ. δόντες Od. 5.38 = Od. 23.341. Cf. Od. 2.339, Od. 7.295, Od. 13.136 = Od. 16.231, Od. 15.77 = 94, Od. 16.389 (with notion of excess), Od. 17.298, 376, Od. 24.486. 3 With copula to be supplied, (it is) enough: ἦ οὐχ ἁ. ὅττι . . .; Il. 5.349, Il. 23.670. Cf. Il. 9.376, Il. 17.450: Od. 2.312.

αλιτροσ.g: [as ἀλιτήμων.] 1 = ἀλιτήμων.: δαίμοσιν (in the eyes of the gods) Il. 23.595. Playfully Od. 5.182. 2 Not showing due regard, showing ill-will Il. 8.361.

αλκαρ.g: τό [ἀλκή.] A means of defence, a safeguard. With dat. of person defended: Τρώεσσιν Il. 5.644. With genit.: Ἀχαιῶν Il. 11.823.

αλκη.g: -ῆς, ἡ [cf. ἄλαλκον.] Dat. ἀλκί (fr. *ἄλξ) Il. 5.299, Il. 13.471, Il. 17.61, etc.: Od. 6.130. 1 Defence, help: οὔτε κλέος οὔτʼ ἀ. Il. 5.532 = Il. 15.564, οὐδέ τις ἀ. γίγνετο (γίγνεται) Il. 21.528: Od. 22.305, οὐδέ τίς ἔστʼ ἀ. Od. 12.120. 2 Prowess in defence or offence, mettle, courage, spirit: συΐ εἴκελος ἀλκήν Il. 4.253. Cf. Il. 3.45, Il. 5.299, Il. 7.164, Il. 9.706, Il. 16.157, Il. 19.36, etc.: ἀλκὶ πεποιθώς Od. 6.130. Cf. Od. 9.214, 514, Od. 17.315, Od. 22.226, 237, Od. 23.128, Od. 24.509. Personified Il. 5.740. 3 Showing of fight, resistance: οὐκ ἀπολήγει ἀλκῆς Il. 21.578. Prowess displayed in action, deeds of prowess, fighting: εἰδότε ἀλκῆς Il. 11.710, ἔπαυσεν ἀλκῆς Il. 15.250. Cf. Od. 13.116, 197, Il. 15.490 (from Zeus), Il. 20.256, etc.: οὐ δεδαηκότες ἀλκήν Od. 2.61. Cf. Od. 4.527. 4 The upper hand, victory: ἀπείρητος οὐδʼ ἀδήριτος ἤ τʼ ἀλκῆς ἤ τε φόβοιο (whether in the matter of . . . or . . . , whether the result be . . . or . . .) Il. 17.42.

αλκτηρ.g: -ῆρος, ὁ [ἀλκ-, ἄλαλκον.] 1 A protector: ἀρῆς (against . . . ) Il. 14.485. Cf. Il. 18.100, 213. 2 A means of protection: κυνῶν Od. 14.531, Od. 21.340.

αλλα.g: [ἄλλος.] 1 Adversative particle, but Il. 1.24, 25, 94, 116, 125, etc.: Od. 1.6, 16, 22, 42, 48, etc. Elliptically: ἀλλʼ οὐ γάρ δʼ ἐθέλω . . . (but I say no more, for . . .) Il. 7.242: ἀλλʼ οὐ γάρ τις πρῆξις ἐγίγνετο (but they soon gave over, for . . . ) Od. 10.202 = 568, ἀλλʼ οὐ γάρ οἱ ἔτʼ ἦν ἴς ἔμπεδος (but it was of no avail, for . . . ) Od. 11.393. Cf. Od. 19.591. 2 Introducing an apodosis, yet, nevertheless: εἴ περ γὰρ . . . ἀλλʼ οὐ πείσονται Il. 8.154. Cf. Il. 1.82, Il. 12.349, Il. 16.38, Il. 24.771, etc.: εἰ . . . ἀλλʼ ἤδη παῖς τοῖος Od. 19.86, etc. Introducing a statement: ἀλλὰ μάλʼ ὤφελλες (why . . . ) Od. 4.472. 3 With imp. (or infin. as imp.) in command, challenge, entreaty, remonstrance, persuasion, encouragement, indignation, etc., nay but, come now ! ἴθι Il. 1.32, πίθεσθε Il. 1.259. Cf. Il. 1.393, Il. 1.508, Il. 1.565, Il. 2.163, 360, etc.: μένʼ αὖθι Od. 2.369, ὧδʼ ἔρδειν Od. 6.258. Cf. Od. 3.323, 380, Od. 4.28, 35, 379, etc. Sim. with subj.: ἴομεν Il. 6.526, etc.: φραζώμεσθα Od. 2.167, φθεγγώμεθα Od. 10.228, etc. With opt.: ἐπιτρέψειας ἕκαστα δμῳάων ἥ τις . . . Od. 15.24. With fut.: ἐρέω Od. 12.156. With ἄνα. See ἄνα1. For ἀλλʼ ἄγε (ἄγετε) see ἄγε.

αλλεγω.g: [ἀλ-, ἀνα-(1) + λέγω2.] Aor. infin. ἀλλέξαι Il. 21.321. To pick up, gather up: ὀστέα Il. 21.321, Il. 23.253.

αλλη.g: [dat. fem. of ἄλλος as adv..] 1 a Elsewhere Il. 13.49: Od. 3.251, Od. 22.140. b ἄλλος ἀ., one in one quarter, one in another Od. 8.516. 2 a Elsewhither, in another direction Il. 1.120, Il. 5.187, Il. 15.464, Il. 21.557: Od. 2.127 = Od. 18.288, Od. 17.478. b In a direction other than the right: ἀ. ἀποκλίναντα (wresting the meaning) Od. 19.556. c ἄλλυδις ἀ., some or part in this direction, some or part in another Od. 5.369, Od. 9.458, Od. 11.385. 3 a Otherwise: εἰ βούλεται ἀ. Il. 15.51. b ἄλλυδις ἀ.: τρέπεται χρὼς ἄλλυδις ἀ. (now to one hue, now to another) Il. 13.279.

αλληκτοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + ληκ-, λήγω.] 1 Unceasing, never still: ἄη νότος Od. 12.325. Unceasing, implacable: θυμόν Il. 9.636. 2 In neut. ἄλληκτον as adv, without intermission or pause: πολεμίζειν Il. 2.452 = Il. 11.12 = Il. 14.152.

αλληλων.g: [redup. fr. ἄλλος.] One another, each other: ἀλλήλοισι κέλευον Il. 2.151. Cf. Il. 3.9, 15, 115, 155, Il. 4.449, 472, 536, etc.: ξεῖνοι ἀλλήλων Od. 1.187. Cf. Od. 1.209, Od. 2.149, Od. 4.620, Od. 5.79, Od. 6.211, Od. 9.55, etc.

αλλογνωτοσ.g: [ἄλλος + γνω-, γιγνώσκω.] App., known to be other; hence, strange, foreign: δήμῳ Od. 2.366.

αλλοδαποσ.g: -ή, -όν [ἄλλος. Second element doubtful.] 1 Foreign, alien Il. 19.324, Il. 24.382: Od. 8.211, Od. 9.36, Od. 14.231, Od. 17.485, Od. 20.220, Od. 23.219. 2 Absol., a foreigner or alien Il. 3.48, Il. 16.550: Od. 3.74 = Od. 9.255.

αλλοειδησ.g: -ές [ἄλλος + εἶδος.] Of another, i. e. of strange, appearance: ἀλλοειδέα φαινέσκετο πάντα Od. 13.194 (ἀ. to be scanned in three long syllables; v. l. ἀλλοειδέʼ ἐφαίνετο).

αλλοθεν.g: [ἄλλος + -θεν 1.] 1 a From another place or source, from elsewhere: ἵνα μή ποθεν ἀ. αὕῃ Od. 5.490, καλεῖ ἀ. Od. 17.382. b ἀ. ἄλλος, some or one from one side or quarter, some or one from another Il. 2.75, Il. 9.311, 671, Il. 13.551: Od. 9.401, 493 = Od. 10.442, Od. 10.119, Od. 11.42, Od. 4.231, Od. 24.415. Sim. νείκεον ἀ. ἄλλον, one beginning with one man, one with another Od. 12.392. 2 From another or strange land, from abroad: εἰλήλουθεν Od. 3.318. Cf. Od. 6.283, Od. 7.33, 52, Od. 16.26, Od. 17.112, Od. 20.360.

αλλοθι.g: [ἄλλος + -θι] 1 In another place, elsewhere Od. 4.684, Od. 16.44, Od. 18.401. On his part, he too: κλαῖεν Od. 21.83. 2 a In another or strange land, abroad: ἐπὴν ἀ. ὄληται Od. 14.130.–ἀ. γαίης, elsewhere in the world, somewhere abroad Od. 2.131. b App., with genit., elsewhere away from (one's home): ἀ. πάτρης (i.e. in some strange land) Od. 17.318.

αλλοθροοσ.g: [ἄλλος + θρόος.] Speaking a strange tongue, foreign, alien Od. 1.183, Od. 3.302, Od. 14.43, Od. 15.453.

αλλοιοσ.g: [ἄλλος.] Of another sort or kind: ἔργῳ Il. 4.258: ἀ. φάνης Od. 16.181, ἄνδρα Od. 19.265.

αλλοπροσαλλοσ.g: [ἄλλος + πρός + ἄλλος.] One thing to one person, another to another, doublefaced Il. 5.831, 889.

αλλοσ.g: -η, -ο. Crasis with τά gives τἆλλα Il. 1.465, Il. 2.428: Od. 3.462, Od. 12.365. I 1 Absol. in sing. a Another or additional person or thing: ἄλλο τοι ἐρέω Il. 1.297, οἴσομεν ἄλλον Il. 3.104. Cf. Il. 10.146, Il. 11.663, Il. 14.262, etc.: Od. 11.454, Od. 12.65, etc. In apposition: ἄλλο τό γε οἶδα Od. 16.470. b α Another or different person or thing, another, someone or something else: ἐγὼ ἢ ἄλλος Ἀχαιῶν Il. 2.231, πείθεόο τʼ ἄλλῳ Il. 2.360. Cf. Il. 2.271, Il. 9.101, Il. 11.410, Il. 13.229, Il. 19.181 (in the case of another matter, i.e. for the future), Il. 24.46, etc.: ἄλλος εἴπεσκε νέων Od. 2.331, μεῖζον ἄλλο φράζονται Od. 4.698. Cf. Od. 3.94, Od. 4.29, Od. 8.202, Od. 11.176, Od. 13.205, Od. 17.404, etc. With τις: ὡς ὄφελέν τις ἀνδρῶν ἄλλος ἔχειν Il. 4.316. Cf. Il. 13.272, Il. 14.90, etc.: ἄλλο τί τοι μελέτω Od. 7.208. Cf. Od. 14.461, Od. 18.334, Od. 20.297, etc. Predicatively: ἄλλο τι τόδε μήδεαι (it is some other thing that you are planning) Od. 5.173. With τίς: τίς τοι ἄλλος ὁμοῖος; Il. 17.475. Cf. Il. 17.586. With the article, the other: ἴἡ ἄλλη σῖτον ἔφερεν Od. 13.69. With οὗτος and τις: ἄλλος τις οὗτος ἀνέστη Od. 20.380. β With the notion of difference obscured, someone. With τις: μή ποτέ τις εἴπῃσι κακώτερος ἄλλος Il. 22.106: Od. 21.324. γ ἄλλο adverbially, app., in another matter Il. 14.249.–(τὸ) ἄλλο τόσον, for the rest to a certain extent, i.e. so far Il. 22.322, Il. 23.454. c In negative or conditional contexts α Any other or additional person or thing. With τις: οὐδέ τις ἄλλος ᾔδεεν Il. 18.403. Cf. Il. 23.592. β Another, any other or different person or thing, any one or anything else: οὐκ ἐθέλεσκες ἅμʼ ἄλλῳ ἰέναι Il. 9.486, εἴ με κελεύεις οἴκοθεν ἄλλʼ ἐπιδοῦναι Il. 23.558. Cf. Il. 14.244, Il. 16.141, Il. 23.274, etc.: οὐδέ κεν ἡμέας ἄλλο διέκρινεν (anything but death) Od. 4.179, etc. With τις: οὔτε σοὶ οὔτε τῳ ἄλλῳ Il. 1.299, εἴ τευ ἐξ ἄλλου γένευ Il. 5.897. Cf. Il. 2.80, Il. 5.827, Il. 9.104, Il. 12.248, Il. 16.225, etc.: εἴ τίς μʼ ἄλλη ἤγγειλεν Od. 23.21. Cf. Od. 6.68, Od. 7.67, Od. 9.520, Od. 10.32, etc. Interrog.: τί σευ ἄλλος ὀνήσεται; Il. 16.31. Cf. Od. 4.649. With τις: πῶς κέν τίς σʼ ἄλλος ἵκοιτο; Od. 9.351. γ With the notion of difference obscured, any one, anything: οὐ σέο κύντερον ἄλλο Il. 8.483, οὐ δύναμαι γλυκερώτερον ἄλλο ἰδέσθαι Od. 9.28. Cf. Od. 11.427, Od. 15.343, 533, Od. 20.392. With τις: οὔ τις σεῖο ὀλοώτερος ἄλλος Il. 3.365. Cf. Il. 15.569, Il. 19.321, Il. 23.439, 580: οὔ τι κύντερον ἄλλο Od. 7.216. Cf. Od. 8.32, 138, Od. 20.201, 376. d Every other, every one, any one, all: ὄφρα στυγέῃ ἄλλος Il. 1.186, ἄλλον κε σεῦ ἀπαλεξήσαιμι Il. 24.370, etc.: ὡς ἀπόλοιτο καὶ ἄλλος ὅτις . . . Od. 1.47, ἄλλῃ νεμεσῶ ἥ τις . . . Od. 6.286, etc. With τις: ἵνα τις στυγέῃσιν ἄλλος Il. 8.515. 2 In sing with sb., etc. a α Another or additional: ἄλλον ὀϊστόν Il. 8.300. Cf. Il. 4.334, Il. 8.309, Il. 15.458, Il. 22.293, Il. 24.551: ἄλλην ὁδόν Od. 10.490, 563. Cf. Od. 15.449. With τις: εἴ τίς μοι ἀνὴρ ἅμʼ ἕποιτο καὶ ἄλλος Il. 10.222. Cf. Od. 10.380, Od. 15.27. β Other, additional: μείζων κʼ ἄλλος χόλος ἐτύχθη (i.e. matters would have gone further) Il. 15.121. γ Besides, in addition: δόλον ἄλλον ὕφαινεν Il. 6.187. Cf. Il. 9.365: τέρας ἄλλο φανήτω Od. 20.101. Cf. Od. 2.93 Od. 24.128–With τις: σῆμʼ ἄλλο τι δείξω (εἴπω) Od. 21.217, Od. 23.73. b α Another or different, some other: πρόμον Il. 7.116. Cf. Il. 3.226, Il. 7.358 = Il. 12.232, Il. 9.423, Il. 14.84, Il. 23.460: ῥάκος ἄλλο (other than his own raiment) Od. 13.434, Od. 14.342. Cf. Od. 3.243, Od. 10.392, Od. 11.127, Od. 15.518, Od. 16.9, Od. 22.6, Od. 23.186, 274. With τις: μή τις Τρῶας ἐγείρῃσιν θεὸς ἄλλος Il. 10.511: δήμόν τι ἄλλο Od. 2.32, 44. Cf. Od. 13.325. β With a collective sb., the other, the rest of the . . . : λαόν Il. 11.189, etc.: δήμῳ Od. 2.239. c In negative or conditional contexts α Any other or additional: υἱὸν οὐ τέκετʼ ἄλλον Il. 5.154. Cf. Il. 19.233. With τις: μηδέ τις ἄλλος ἴτω ἀνήρ Il. 24.148 = 177. Cf. Il. 24.505: Od. 5.179 = Od. 10.344, Od. 5.187,

αλλοτε.g: [ἄλλος + ὅτε.] 1 At another time, at other times Il. 10.120, Il. 13.776, Il. 19.200, Il. 20.53, Il. 22.171, Il. 24.511. 2 Repeated: ἀ. . . ἀ. . . ., at one time . . . at another . . ., now . . . now . . . Il. 5.595, Il. 18.159, 472, Il. 21.464, Il. 23.368, Il. 24.530: Od. 4.102, Od. 5.331, Od. 11.303, Od. 16.209, Od. 23.94. Thrice (followed by τοτέ) Il. 24.10. Sim. ὁτὲ . . . ἀ . . . Il. 11.65, Il. 18.602, Il. 20.50.– ἀ . . . .ὁτὲ . . . Il. 11.566. 3 With ἄλλος: ἀ. ἐπʼ ἄλλον (now on to one, now on to another) Il. 15.684: ἀ. ἄλλῳ (now to one, now to another) Od. 4.236. 4 At another time, on a former occasion: ἀ. με ῥίψεν Il. 1.590. Cf. Il. 20.90, 187.

αλλοτριοσ.g: -η, -ον [ἄλλος.] 1 Of or belonging to others, not one's own Il. 20.298: Od. 1.160, Od. 9.535, Od. 11.115, Od. 18.280, Od. 19.119, Od. 20.171, 221, Od. 24.301. As if not one's own: γναθμοῖσι γελώων ἀλλοτρίοισιν Od. 20.347 (not expressing their real feelings). Absol. in neut. pl., things of others, what is not one's own: ἀλλοτρίων χαρίσασθαι Od. 17.452. Cf. Od. 17.456, Od. 18.18. 2 Foreign, alien Il. 5.214: = Od. 16.102, Od. 14.86, Od. 18.219.

αλλοφοσ.g: -ον [ἀ-1 + λόφος.] Having no crest: κυνέην Il. 10.258.

αλλοφρονεων.g: -οντος [ a first element poss. conn. with ἠλεός + φρονέω.] Dazed, 'silly' Il. 23.698. Troubled or dashed in spirit Od. 10.374.

αλλυδισ.g: [ἄλλος.] Elsewhither, in another direction. 1 ἀ. ἄλλος, some or part in this direction, some or part in another Il. 11.486, 745, Il. 12.461, Il. 17.729, Il. 21.503: Od. 5.71, Od. 6.138, Od. 14.25, 35. 2 ἀ. ἄλλῃ. See ἄλλῃ 2.c, 3.b.

αλλωσ.g: [ἄλλος.] 1 Otherwise, differently, so as to bring about a different result Il. 14.53. In other circumstances Od. 15.513. Reversing a previous decision: μετεβούλευσαν Od. 5.286. 2 In some other form: εἰ ἀ. δοίης δωτίνην Od. 9.267. For some other reason Od. 17.577. In novel fashion: ἑψιάασθαι Od. 8.429. 3 καὶ ἀ., as it is, at the best of times, without that: ἀγήνωρ ἐστὶ καὶ ἀ. Il. 9.699. Cf. Il. 20.99: Od. 21.87. 4 Otherwise (connoting improvement): πάρος οὐκ ἔσσεται ἀ. Il. 5.218. In other and better wise, better, more effectually: σαωσέμεν Il. 19.401. Cf. Il. 11.391: οὔ κεν ἀ. θεὸς τεύξειεν Od. 8.176. Cf. Od. 20.211, Od. 24.107. 5 Otherwise than with due regard to truth, idly, at random: ἀ. ψεύδονται Od. 14.124. 6 With other result than that hoped for, in vain, fruitlessly: ἀ. ἠρήσατο Il. 23.144.

αλμα.g: -ατος, τό [ἅλλομαι.] Jumping, leaping Od. 8.128. In pl.: περιγιγνόμεθʼ ἄλλων ἅλμασιν Od. 8.103.

αλμη.g: -ης, ἡ [ἅλς2.] 1 Sea-water, brine Od. 5.53, 322. 2 Dried sea-spray Od. 6.137, 219, 225, Od. 23.237.

αλογεω.g: [ἀ-1 + λογ-, λέγω2.] To pay no heed or regard Il. 15.162, 178.

αλοιφη.g: -ῆς, ἡ [ἀλείφω.] 1 Unguent, oil Od. 6.220, Od. 18.179. Tallow applied to a bow Od. 8.179. 2 Oil or grease used for dressing a hide Il. 17.390, 392. 3 Hog's lard or grease: συὸς ῥάχιν τεθαλυῖαν ἀλοιθῇ Il. 9.208. Cf. Il. 9.467, 32: Od. 8.476, Od. 13.410.

αλοσυδνη.g: -ης [sense unknown. Traditionally explained as 'daughter of the sea' (ἅλς1).] Of Thetis Il. 20.207. Of Amphitrite Od. 4.404.

αλσ1.g: ἁλός, ἡ [σαλ-. Cf. L. sal.] As genit. ἁλόσεν Il. 21.335. The sea Il. 1.141, 316, 350, 358, Il. 2.626, etc.: Od. 1.162, Od. 3.73, Od. 4.580, 844, Od. 13.235, etc.

αλσ2.g: ἁλός, ὁ [cf. ἅλς1.] Dat. pl. ἅλεσσι Od. 11.123, Od. 23.270. 1 Salt Il. 9.214. In pl.: ἅλεσσι μεμιγμένον εἶδαρ Od. 11.123 = Od. 23.270. 2 A piece of salt Od. 17.455.

αλσοσ.g: τό. 1 A grove Il. 20.8: Od. 10.350, Od. 17.208. 2 A sacred grove: Ὀγχηστόν, Ποσιδήϊον ἀ. (i.e. O. with its grove) Il. 2.506: Ἀθήνης Od. 6.291. Cf. Od. 6.321, Od. 9.200, Od. 10.509, Od. 20.278.

αλυσκαζω.g: [ἀλύσκω.] 1 To escape, avoid: ὕβριν Od. 17.581. 2 Absol., to play the shirker Il. 5.253, Il. 6.443.

αλυσκω.g: 3 sing. fut. ἀλύξει Od. 17.547, Od. 19.558. Infin. ἀλύξειν Il. 10.371. Aor. ἤλυξα Od. 12.335. 3 sing. ἤλυξε Il. 11.476. ἄλυξε Od. 23.332. 3 pl. ἤλυξαν Od. 3.297. ἄλυξαν Od. 23.328. 2 sing. subj. ἀλύξῃς Od. 11.113, Od. 12.140. 3 sing. -ῃ Il. 10.348: Od. 22.66. 1 pl. opt. ἀλύξαιμεν Od. 10.269. Pple. ἀλύξας Il. 12.113, Il. 13.395, Il. 15.287: Od. 2.352, Od. 5.387, Od. 8.353. Infin. ἀλύξαι Il. 8.243, Il. 21.565, Il. 22.201: Od. 4.416, Od. 5.345, Od. 12.216, Od. 22.460. (ὑπ-.) 1 To escape, evade, avoid (impending danger): ὄλεθρον Il. 10.371. Cf. Il. 11.476, Il. 12.113, Il. 13.395, Il. 15.287, Il. 21.565: κῆρας Od. 2.352 = Od. 5.387. Cf. Od. 3.297, Od. 10.269, Od. 12.216, Od. 17.547 = Od. 19.558, Od. 22.66, 363, 382, Od. 23.328, 332. 2 To get away from, effect one's escape or release from (something in which one is involved): χρέος καὶ δεσμόν (getting out of the debt and freeing himself from the bonds) Od. 8.353. To get free from the company of: ἑταίρους Od. 12.335. 3 Absol., to effect one's escape, escape, save oneself Il. 21.243, Il. 10.348, Il. 22.201: Od. 4.416, Od. 5.345, Od. 11.113 = Od. 12.140, Od. 22.460.

αλυτοσ.g: -ον [ἀ-1 + λύω.] Not to be loosed: πέδας Il. 13.37, πεῖραρ 360: δεσμούς Od. 8.275.

αλυω.g: ( υ Od. 9.398). 1 To be beside oneself from pain or grief: ἀλύουσʼ ἀπεβήσετο Il. 5.352. Cf. Il. 24.12. From exultation Od. 18.333 = 393. 2 To manifest distraction by gestures: χερσὶν ἀλύων Od. 9.398.

αλφεσιβοιοσ.g: -η [ἀλθε-, ἀλθάνω + -σι- + βοῦς.] Bringing (her parents many) oxen (as bride-price) Il. 18.593.

αλφηστησ.g: -οῦ [ἀλθ-, ἀλθάνω.] Epithet of men, gain-getting, having to labour for their bread Od. 1.349, Od. 6.8, Od. 13.261.

αλφιτον.g: -ου, τό. Barley (i.e. the prepared corn): ἀλθίτου ἀκτήν (barley-meal) Il. 11.631. Cf. Od. 2.355, Od. 14.429. In pl.: ἄλθιτα λευκά Il. 11.640. Cf. Il. 18.560: Od. 2.290, 354, 380, Od. 10.234, 520, Od. 11.28, Od. 14.77, Od. 19.197, Od. 20.108, 119.

αλωη.g: -ῆς, ἡ. 1 A threshing-floor Il. 5.499, Il. 13.588, Il. 20.496. 2 A piece of levelled or prepared ground, a garden, orchard, vineyard Il. 5.90, Il. 9.534, 540, Il. 18.57 = 438, Il. 21.36, 77, 346: Od. 6.293. Distinguished as an orchard Od. 24.221, 224, 226, 336. As a vineyard Il. 18.561, 566 (in both cases referring to a representation in metal): Od. 1.193, Od. 7.122, Od. 11.193.

αμα.g: [σα-. Cf. ἀ-2, ἅπαξ, ἅπας, ἁπλοΐς, L. simul.] I Adv. 1 With, along with, a person or persons, in his or their company: ἁ. ἕποντο Il. 1.424, θέρει ἁ. παῖδα Il. 6.389. Cf. Il. 3.447, Il. 4.274, Il. 9.170, Il. 10.194, Il. 11.344, etc.: κήρυχʼ ἁ. ὀπάσσας Od. 9.90. Cf. Od. 2.287, 413, Od. 6.319, Od. 8.109, Od. 13.68, etc. 2 All or both together, in a body, without exception: πάντες ἁ. Il. 1.495, ταῦθʼ ἁ. χρὴ σπεύδειν (with united effort) Il. 13.235. Cf. Il. 1.533, Il. 6.59, Il. 8.8, Il. 15.718, Il. 18.50, etc.: ἁ. πλέομεν Od. 3.276. Cf. Od. 8.121, Od. 10.259, Od. 11.232, Od. 12.110, Od. 13.82, etc. In reference to things, all at once, without exception: ἁ. πάνθʼ ἑλέσθαι Il. 13.729. Cf. Il. 4.320. 3 At the same time: σκεψάμενος ἐς νῆʼ ἁ. καὶ μεθʼ ἑταίρους Od. 12.247. Cf. Od. 10.123, Od. 18.356. Together, at the same moment: ἁ. ἄμφω σύν ῥʼ ἔπεσον Il. 7.255. Cf. Il. 13.613, Il. 19.242, etc.: ὁμαρτήσαντες ἁ. ἄμφω Od. 8.188. In reference to something done while others are doing other things: τῇ ἁ. Ἀ. κλισίην ἔθηκεν, Ἀ. δὲ . . . Φ. δὲ . . . Od. 4.123. 4 At the same time, besides, too, also: ἁ. δʼ ἄλλʼ ἀποδάσσεσθαι Il. 22.117. Cf. Il. 24.304: Od. 19.376.–ἁ. . . . καὶ . . . , both . . . and . . . : ἁ. πρόσσω καὶ ὀπίσσω Il. 1.343. Cf. Il. 2.707, Il. 13.299, etc.: Od. 3.111, Od. 19.471, etc. So ἁ. . . . τε . . . καὶ . . . Od. 24.249.– ἁ. τε . . . τε Il. 13.669.– ἁ. τε . . . δὲ . . . Il. 9.519.– Other combinations in Il. 1.417, Il. 2.281, Il. 4.450, Il. 13.85, Il. 24.773, etc.: Od. 14.403. II Prep. with dat. (freq. following the case). 1 With, along with, in company with: ἁ. ἡγεμόνεσσιν Il. 3.1. Cf. Il. 1.158, 226, 251, Il. 2.249, 524, etc.: τῷ ἁ. πομπὸν ἕπεσθαι Od. 4.162. Cf. Od. 1.98, 331, 428, Od. 2.11, Od. 3.359, etc. 2 At the same time with, at the time of: ἁ. ἠελίῳ καταδύντι Il. 1.592. Cf. Il. 7.331, Il. 9.618, Il. 11.685, Il. 18.136, Il. 24.600, etc.: ἁ. ἠοῖ Od. 4.407. Cf. Od. 6.31, Od. 12.24, Od. 14.266, Od. 16.2, Od. 23.362, etc.

αμαθοσ.g: [cf. ψάμαθος.] Loose or sandy soil Il. 5.587.

αμαθυνω.g: [ἄμαθος.] To level with the dust, destroy: πόλιν Il. 9.593.

αμαιμακετοσ.g: -η, -ον [perh. redup. fr. μακ-, μακρός.] Thus, of very great size or height: χίμαιραν Il. 6.179, Il. 16.329: ἱστὸν νηός Od. 14.311.

αμαλδυνω.g: Aor. pple. ἀμαλδύνας Il. 12.32. Infin. ἀμαλδῦναι Il. 12.18. To destroy, level Il. 7.463, Il. 12.18, 32.

αμαλλοδετηρ.g: -ῆρος [ἄμαλλα, sheaf + δέω.] A binder of sheaves Il. 18.553, 554.

αμαλοσ.g: -ή. Of young animals, tender, feeble: ἄρνα Il. 22.310: σκυλάκεσσιν Od. 20.14.

αμαρτη.g: [ἅμα + ἀρ-, ἀραρίσκω.] 1 Both or all together: δούρατʼ ἤϊξαν Il. 5.656, ῥήσσοντες Il. 18.571. 2 At the same moment, simultaneously Il. 21.162: Od. 22.81.

αμαρτοεπησ.g: [ἁμαρτάνω + ἔπος. Cf. ἁμαρτοεπής.] Stumbling in speech. In voc. ἁμαρτοεπές Il. 13.824.

αματροχιη.g: -ῆς, ἡ [ἅμα + τροχ-, τρέχω.] A coming of wheels together, a coming of chariots abreast of each other Il. 23.422.

αμαω1.g: (ἀπ-, δι-.) 1 To reap, act as reaper Il. 18.551. 2 To reap (a crop) Od. 9.135. To cut (reeds) Il. 24.451. 3 To slice off: ἀπʼ οὔατʼ ἀμήσαντες Od. 8.301.

αμαω2.g: [perh. conn. with ἅμα.] (ὲπ-, κατ-.) To collect, bring together. In mid. : ἐν ταλάροισιν ἀμησάμενος Od. 9.247.

αμβατοσ.g: -όν [ἀμ-, ἀνα- 1 + βα-, βαίνω.] Capable of being scaled: πόλις Il. 6.434: οὐρανός Od. 11.316.

αμβληδην.g: [ἀμβλη-, ἀμβάλλω = ἀναβάλλω.] Lifting up the voice Il. 22.476. (Cf. ἀνεβάλλετʼ ἀείδειν under ἀναβάλλω 2.)

αμβολαδην.g: [ἀμβολ-, ἀμβάλλω. See ἀμβλήδην.] Spirting up: λέβης ζεῖ ἀ. Il. 21.364.

αμβροσιη.g: -ης, ἡ [fem. of ἀμβρόσιος. as sb. Fragrance.] 1 The food of the gods Od. 5.93, 199, Od. 9.359, Od. 12.63. Introduced into Achilles Il. 19.347, 353. Eaten by divine horses Il. 5.777. 2 Used as a perfume Od. 4.445. By Here as a cleansing (and doubtless perfuming) cosmetic Il. 14.170. Applied by divine agency as a preservative or for purification to the corpse of Sarpedon Il. 16.670, 680. Introduced by divine agency into the corpse of Patroclus Il. 19.38.

αμβροσιοσ.g: -η, -ον. Sweet-smelling, fragrant: χαῖται Il. 1.529, νύκτα Il. 2.57 (prob. referring to the fragrance of a still warm night), ὕπνος Il. 2.19 (prob. a transference of epithet from νύξ). Cf. Il. 5.338, 369, Il. 8.434, Il. 10.41, 142, Il. 13.35, Il. 14.172, 177, 178, Il. 18.268, Il. 21.507, Il. 23.187 (here no doubt with a reference to preservative properties of the divine food; cf. ἀμβροσίη 2), Il. 24.341, 363: = Od. 1.97 = Od. 5.45, Od. 4.429 = 574, Od. 7.283, Od. 9.404, Od. 15.8, Od. 18.193.

αμβροτοσ1.g: -ον. = ἀμβρόσιος.: εἵματα Il. 16.670, 680: Od. 7.260, 265, Od. 24.59, ἐλαίῳ Od. 8.365, νύξ Od. 11.330.

αμβροτοσ2.g: [ἀ-1 + (μ)βροτός.] 1 Immortal Il. 20.358, Il. 22.9, Il. 24.460: Od. 24.445. Of horses Il. 16.381 = 867. 2 Of or belonging to a god, divine Il. 5.339, 870: Od. 5.347. 3 Befitting a god Il. 17.194, 202: Od. 10.222. 4 App., conferring divine qualities: δῶρα Od. 18.191.

αμεγαρτοσ.g: -ον [ἀ-1 + μεγαίρω.] Not to be envied or desired. 1 Of a person in depreciation, miserable, wretched Od. 17.219, Od. 8.362. 2 Dread, dire Il. 2.420: Od. 11.400 = 407.

αμειβοντεσ.g: οἱ [pres. pple. pl. of ἀμείβω.] The rafters, sloping to each other in pairs, of a pitched roof Il. 23.712 (the wrestlers, with shoulders together but standing wide apart with their feet, being compared with a pair).

αμειβω.g: 3 sing. aor. mid. ἠμείψατο Il. 23.542. ἀμείψατο Il. 4.403. 3 sing. subj. ἀμείψεται Il. 9.409: Od. 10.328. Pple. ἀμειψάμενος Od. 24.285. Infin. ἀμείψασθαι Il. 23.489: Od. 2.83, Od. 4.286, Od. 16.91. (ἀπ-, ἐπ-, παρ-.) 1 To change: ἔντεα Il. 17.192. To exchange (with another). With genit. of what is taken in exchange: τεύχεα πρὸς Διομήδεα χρύσεα χαλκείων Il. 6.235. Sim., to exchange (the support of) one thing for (that of) another: γόνυ γουνός Il. 11.547. 2 To cause persons to exchange: τεύχεα Il. 14.381. 3 In mid. a To requite: εὖ σε δώροισιν ἀμειψάμενος (making a good return to you in gifts) Od. 24.285. b To take turns with one another: ἀμειβόμενοι θυλακὰς ἔχον Il. 9.471. So ἀμειβόμεναι ὀπὶ καλῇ (taking up the strain from each other) Il. 1.604: Od. 24.60.– ἀμειβόμενοι κατὰ οἴκους (each in turn giving the feast in his house) Od. 1.375 = Od. 2.140.– ταρφέʼ ἀμειβομένω (with frequent change (from side to side)) Od. 8.379. c To pass from one position or place to another: ἄλλοτʼ ἐπʼ ἄλλον [ἵππον] ἀμείβεται Il. 15.684. d To pass from, leave, quit: ἕρκος ὀδόντων Il. 9.409. e To enter: ἕρκος ὀδόντων Od. 10.328. f To answer, reply to Il. 1.121, 172, 292, 413, etc.: Od. 1.44, Od. 2.83, Od. 3.102, Od. 4.286, etc.– g To speak in answer, make answer Il. 13.823, Il. 23.489, 492, Il. 24.200, 424: Od. 3.148, Od. 4.382, 484, Od. 6.67, etc. In pres. pple. ἀμειβόμενος, -η, making answer, in answer Il. 3.437, Il. 7.356, Il. 14.270, etc.: Od. 2.84, Od. 4.234, 375, etc.

αμειλιχοσ.g: [as ἀμείλικτος.] Inflexible, implacable, relentless: Ἀΐδης Il. 9.158, ἦτορ 572, ἄνακτος Il. 24.734.

αμεινων.g: -ονος. Neut. ἄμεινον. Acc. sing. masc. and fem. ἀμείνω Il. 3.11, Il. 4.400, Il. 9.423. Neut. pl. ἀμείνω Od. 7.310, Od. 15.71. Used as comp. of ἀγαθός or ἐσθλός. 1 More warlike, soldierly, or skilful in fight Il. 2.239, Il. 4.405, Il. 5.173, 411, Il. 6.479, Il. 7.111, 114, Il. 15.641, Il. 16.709, Il. 21.107, Il. 22.158, 333: Od. 18.334. So βίην ἀ. Il. 1.404, Il. 15.139.– βιῃ ἀ. Il. 11.787. 2 Better, more worthy, serviceable or skilful: ἀγορῇ Il. 4.400. Cf. Il. 6.350, Il. 18.106, Il. 23.315, 479, 605 (your betters): Od. 2.180, Od. 7.51, Od. 22.156. In reference to personal appearance Od. 24.374. Of horses Il. 10.556. 3 Of things or abstractions, better of their kind, better, more excellent, helpful or in place: ὀμίχλην νυκτὸς ἀμείνω Il. 3.11. Cf. Il. 1.116, Il. 7.358 = Il. 12.232, Il. 9.104, 256, 423, Il. 12.412, Il. 14.107, Il. 15.509: ἀμείνω αἴσιμα πάντα Od. 7.310, Od. 15.71. Cf. Od. 1.376 = Od. 2.141, Od. 5.364, Od. 14.466, Od. 22.374. Impers. with infin.: πείθεσθαι ἄμεινόν [ἐστιν] Il. 1.274. Cf. Il. 11.469: Od. 22.104. Sim.: ὧς γὰρ ἄμεινον Il. 1.217. 4 Good rather than ill: οὔ οἱ τό γʼ ἄμεινον Il. 24.52.

αμελγω.g: (ἐν-.) To milk Od. 9.238, 244 = 341, 308. In pass. with the milk in acc.: ἀμελγόμεναι γάλα Il. 4.434.

αμελεω.g: [ἀ-1 + μέλω.] With genit. (and always with neg.). 1 To disregard the claims of, fail to aid: οὐκ ἀμέλησε κασιγνήτοιο Il. 8.330. Cf. Il. 13.419. In sinister sense of holding back from attempting to despoil Il. 17.9. 2 To disregard, fail to carry out: ἐθημοσύνης Il. 17.697.

αμενηνοσ.g: [ἀ-1. App. obscurely conn. with μένος.] Weak, powerless Il. 5.887. Of ghosts, fleeting, feeble Od. 10.521, 536, Od. 11.29, 49. Of dreams, fleeting, transient Od. 19.562.

αμενηνοω.g: [ἀμενηνός.] To deprive of efficiency or effect: αἰχμήν Il. 13.562.

αμερδω.g: 3 sing. aor. ἄμερσε Od. 8.64. Infin. ἀμέρσαι Il. 16.53. 2 sing. aor. subj. pass. ἀμερθῇς Il. 22.58. 1 To deprive of or debar from. With genit.: αἰῶνος Il. 22.58. Cf. Od. 8.64, Od. 8.290. 2 To despoil, rob Il. 16.53. 3 To blind (the eyes) Il. 13.340. 4 To deprive of lustre, tarnish Od. 19.18.

αμετρητοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + μετρέω.] Immeasurable, endless: πένθος Od. 19.512, πόνος Od. 23.249.

αμετροεπησ.g: [ἀ-1 + μέτρον + ἔπος.] Unmeasured in words. Of Thersites Il. 2.212.

αμηχανοσ.g: -ον [ἀ-1 + μηχανή = μῆχος.] 1 Without resources, helpless Od. 19.363. 2 Unmanageable, difficult to deal with: ἀ. παραρρητοῖσι πιθέσθαι (in that you will not listen to persuasion) Il. 13.726. Of Here Il. 15.14. Of Achilles Il. 16.29. Of Agamemnon Il. 19.273. Playfully of Nestor Il. 10.167. Against which no contrivance avails Il. 8.130 = Il. 11.310. Impracticable, not to be attempted Il. 14.262. Difficult to deal with or expound: ὄνειροι Od. 19.560.

αμιτροχιτωνεσ.g: [ἀ-1 + μίτρη + χιτών.] Wearing no μίτρη with the χιτών, not wearing theμίτρη Il. 16.419.

αμιχθαλοεισ.g: -εσσα [prob. = ὀμιχθαλόεις fr. ὀμίχλη.] Thus, misty, steaming. Of Lemnos Il. 24.753. (Lemnos is not volcanic. The reference may be to some jet of natural gas which has now disappeared.)

αμμοριη.g: -ης, ἡ [ἄμμορος.] App., what (of good) fate does not bestow, ill fortune Od. 20.76.

αμμοροσ.g: -ον [ἀ-1 + μόρος.] 1 Denied the just dues of mankind, ill - fated Il. 6.408, Il. 24.773. 2 Having no share in, not entering. With genit.: λοετρῶν Ὠκεανοῖο Il. 18.489: = Od. 5.275.

αμνιον.g: τό [app. conn. with αἷμα.] A vessel for collecting the blood of a sacrificial victim Od. 3.444.

αμοθεν.g: [ἁμός = τις + -θεν 1.] From any point (of a narrative): τῶν ἁ. εἰπέ Od. 1.10.

αμοιβασ.g: [ἀμείβω.] Of a garment, kept for a change (= ἐπημοιβός 1): χλαῖνα Od. 14.521.

αμοιβη.g: -ῆς, ἡ [ἀμείβω.] 1 A return or requital: ἄξιον ἔσται ἀμοιβῆς (will bring a (full) return) Od. 1.318, ἑκατόμβης (for . . . ) Od. 3.58. 2 Compensation: βοῶν (for the loss of . . . ) Od. 12.382.

αμοιβοι.g: οἱ [ἀμοιβή.] A relieving force: ἦλθον ἀμοιβοί (as a . . . ) Il. 13.793.

αμολγοσ.g: Sense unknown. (ἐν) νυκτὸς ἀμολγῷ, gen. rendered, in the depth or gloom of night Il. 11.173, Il. 15.324, Il. 22.28, 317: Od. 4.841. (But Sirius, referred to in Il. 22.27 as shining ὀπώρης, is not then seen in the depth of night; and ἀστὴρ ἕσπερος in Il. 22.317 also causes difficulty.)

αμοσ.g: -ή, -όν. Our ( = ἡμέτερος) Il. 6.414, Il. 8.178, Il. 10.448, Il. 13.96, Il. 16.830: Od. 11.166 = 481. (But the sense my (cf. ἡμέτερος 2) is always admissible, and in Il. 6.414, and perh. in Il. 8.178, is preferable.)

αμοτοσ.g: In neut. ἄμοτον as adv., insatiably, continually, incessantly, without pause or intermission Il. 4.440, Il. 5.518, Il. 13.40, 80, Il. 19.300, Il. 22.36, Il. 23.567: Od. 6.83, Od. 17.520.

αμπελοεισ.g: -εσσα [ἄμπελος.] Rich in vines. Epithet of places Il. 2.561, Il. 3.184, Il. 9.152 = 294.

αμπερεσ.g: [ἀμπείρω.] Passing through. With διά (cf. διαμπερές): διὰ δʼ ἀ. ἰὸς κατέπηκτο Il. 11.377. Cf. Il. 17.309: Od. 21.422.

αμπηδαω.g: [ἀμ-, ἀνα- 1.] To leap up, start up: ἐκ λόχου ἀμπήδησεν Il. 11.379.

αμπυξ.g: -υκος. A diadem of metal worn over the forehead Il. 22.469.

αμυδισ.g: [ἅμα.] 1 Together, all together, in or into a body or mass: θυνόντων ἀ. Il. 10.524. Cf. Il. 9.6, Il. 10.300, Il. 12.385, Il. 13.336, 343, Il. 20.114, 158, 374, Il. 23.217: Od. 4.659, Od. 12.413. 2 Together, at the same time: ἀ. βρόντησε καὶ ἔμβαλε κεραυνόν Od. 12.415 = Od. 14.305. Cf. Od. 5.467.

αμυμων.g: -ονος. 1 An epithet of persons of general commendation, noble, illustrious, goodly, or the like: μάντις Il. 1.92, Αἰθιοπῆας 423. Cf. Il. 2.674, Il. 5.247, Il. 6.155, Il. 11.835, Il. 20.236, etc.: Αἰγίσθοιο (app. as a merely conventional epithet) Od. 1.29, Ὀδυσῆος Od. 2.225. Cf. Od. 4.187, Od. 7.29, Od. 8.117, Od. 19.332, Od. 8.325, etc. Of women: ἄκοιτιν Il. 6.374. Cf. Od. 4.4, Od. 7.303, Od. 13.42, Od. 15.15, etc. Of a nymph Il. 14.444. Of a horse Il. 16.152. 2 Sim. of things or abstractions, indicating excellence or perfection: πομπῇ Il. 6.171, ἔργα Il. 9.128, τόξῳ Il. 15.463. Cf. Il. 9.270, Il. 10.19, Il. 13.637, Il. 16.119, Il. 19.245, Il. 23.263: οἶκος Od. 1.232, μῆτις Od. 9.414. Cf. Od. 10.50, Od. 12.261, Od. 14.508, Od. 16.237, Od. 22.442 = 459, Od. 23.145, Od. 24.80, 278. 3 Absol. in neut. pl.: δς ἂν ἀμύμονα εἰδῇ (is of noble heart) (see εἴδω III.12) Od. 19.332.

αμυντωρ.g: -ορος, ὁ [ἀμύνω.] A defender or helper Il. 14.449, Il. 15.540, 610: Od. 2.326, Od. 16.256, 261.

αμυνω.g: 3 sing. impf. ἄμυνε Il. 13.678, Il. 14.71, Il. 15.731. 3 sing. aor. ἤμυνε Il. 9.599, Il. 13.783. ἄμυνε Il. 4.129, Il. 5.662, Il. 12.402, Il. 17.615. 3 sing. opt. ἀμύναι Il. 12.334, Il. 15.736. Imp. ἄμυνον Il. 1.456, Il. 15.375: Od. 22.208. Infin. ἀμῦναι Il. 1.67, Il. 9.576, Il. 16.75, Il. 24.489, etc.: Od. 2.59, Od. 17.538. Aor. opt. mid. ἀμυναίμην Od. 2.62, Od. 12.114. (ἀπ-, ἐπ-, προσ-.) 1 To ward off, keep off, avert: λοιγόν Il. 5.603, 662, Il. 18.450, Il. 20.98. Il. 24.489. Cf. Il. 6.463, Il. 9.599, Il. 13.783, Il. 15.375, Il. 17.615: ἀρήν Od. 2.59 = Od. 17.538, Od. 22.208, μνηστῆρας Od. 24.380. To defend oneself against, fight with: δήϊον ἄνδρα Il. 22.84. With dat. of person or thing protected: ἡμῖν λοιγόν Il. 1.67. Cf. Il. 1.341, 398, 456, Il. 4.129, Il. 9.435, 495, Il. 11.277, 588, Il. 12.334, Il. 13.426, Il. 15.736, Il. 16.32, 512, 835, Il. 17.511, Il. 18.129, Il. 20.124: ἄστεϊ νηλεὲς ἦμαρ Od. 8.525. With genit. : κῆρας παιδός Il. 12.402. Cf. Il. 4.11, Il. 15.731, Il. 16.75, 80. 2 To defend, protect, succour, fight for, come to the rescue of. With dat.: ὤρεσσιν Il. 5.486, σοῖσιν ἔτῃσιν Il. 6.262. Cf. Il. 9.518, 602, Il. 11.674, Il. 13.464, 481, Il. 14.71, 362, 369, Il. 15.73, 255, 492 (supplying αὐτοῖς), 688, Il. 16.265, Il. 17.273, 563, 703, Il. 21.215, 231, 414: Ἀργείοισιν Od. 11.500, 518. Cf. Od. 16.257, Od. 21.195, 197, Od. 22.214. With genit.: οὗ παιδός Il. 16.522. Cf. Il. 13.109. 3 Absol. to play the defender, fight, show fight: ἐξελθεῖν καὶ ἀμῦναι Il. 9.576. Cf. Il. 13.312, 678, 814, Il. 17.182: οὐ τοῖοι ἀμυνέμεν Od. 2.60. 4 In mid. a To ward or keep off from oneself: ἀμύνετο νηλεὲς ἦμαρ Il. 11.484, Il. 13.514. Cf. Il. 17.510. Sim. ἄνδρας θηρητῆρας ἀμύνονται πεπρὶ τέκνων Il. 12.170. To defend oneself against, fight with: σκύλλην Od. 12.114. b To defend, protect, fight for. With genit.: Καλυδῶνος Il. 9.531. Cf. Il. 12.155, 179, Il. 16.561. With ablative: ναῦφιν Il. 13.700. c Absol., to play the defender, fight: περὶ νηῶν Il. 12.142. Cf. Il. 12.227, 243, Il. 15.496, Il. 16.556, 622, Il. 18.173, Il. 24.500: ἧός μοι ἀμύνεσθαι πάρʼ ὀϊστοί Od. 22.106. Cf. Od. 2.62, Od. 22.116.

αμυσσω.g: 2 sing. fut. ἀμύξεις Il. 1.243. (κατ-.) To tear, lacerate: χερσὶ στήθεα Il. 19.284. Fig.: θυμόν Il. 1.243.

αμφαγαπαζω.g: [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] 1 To welcome (with suppressed notion of embracing) Od. 14.381. 2 To show love to, treat with affection. In mid. Il. 16.192.

αμφαδα.g: [ἀμφαίνω = ἀναφαίνω.] Openly, without concealment: μὴ ἀ. ἔργα γένοιτο (disclosure should take place) Od. 19.391.

αμφαδιοσ.g: [as ἀμφαδά.] 1 Open, public: γάμον Od. 6.288. 2 Adv. of acc. fem. form ἀμφαδίην = ἀμφαδά. Il. 7.196, Il. 13.356: Od. 5.120.

αμφαδον.g: [as ἀμφάδιος.] Openly, without concealment or subterfuge: βαλέειν Il. 7.243, ἀγορευέμεν Il. 9.370: ἠὲ δόλῳ ἢ ἀ. Od. 1.296, Od. 11.120, ἢ ἀ. ἦε κρυφηδόν Od. 14.330 = Od. 19.299.

αμφαραβεω.g: [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] To rattle or ring about one: τεύχεʼ ἀμφαράβησεν Il. 21.408.

αμφασιη.g: ἡ [ἀμ- (= ἀ-1) + φα-, φημί.] Speechlessness: ἀ. μιν λάβεν Il. 17.695: = Od. 4.704.

αμφηκησ.g: Neut. ἄμφηκες. [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 2 + ἀκή, point, edge.] Two-edged Il. 10.256, Il. 21.118: Od. 16.80, Od. 8.341.

αμφηρεφησ.g: [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 1 + ἐρέφω.] Covering on both sides: φαρέτρην (i.e. enclosing (the arrows)) Il. 1.45.

αμφηριστοσ.g: [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 1 + ἐρίζω.] Disputed on both sides. In neut. qualifying a vague notion the state of things; hence, a dead heat: ἀμφήριστόν κʼ ἔθηκεν Il. 23.382, 527.

αμφι.g: I Adv. 1 a On both sides: ἀ. ὀβελοῖσιν ἔπειραν (so that the spits appeared on both sides) Il. 1.465 = Il. 2.428. Cf. Il. 9.210: ξύλα τʼ ἀ. καὶ οἰσέμεν ὕδωρ (i.e. to be set on either side of the altar) Od. 3.429. Cf. Od. 3.462 = Od. 12.365 = Od. 14.430, Od. 14.75. b In reference to the two sides of the body: ἀ. ὄσσε νὺξ ἐκάλυψεν (both eyes) Il. 5.310 = Il. 11.356. Cf. Il. 6.117, Il. 10.535, etc.: δρεψαμένω ἀ. δειράς Od. 2.153. Cf. Od. 9.389. Sim. in reference to the φρένες (see μέλας 1): μένεος φρένες ἀ. μελαιναι πίμπλαντο Il. 1.103: = Od. 4.661. Cf. Il. 17.83, 499, 573. From side to side: ἀ. μοι χεὶρ ὀδύνῃσιν ἐλήλαται Il. 16.517. 2 Round, about, round about: ἔστασαν Il. 4.330. Cf. Il. 4.328, Il. 5.194, Il. 7.449, Il. 11.417, Il. 14.420, etc.: χλαίνας βάλον Od. 4.50. Cf. Od. 3.32, Od. 4.253, Od. 5.72, Od. 7.14, Od. 9.22, etc. Joined with περί Il. 21.10, Il. 23.191. Fig.: ἀ. μάλα φράζεσθε (look at the matter all round, consider well) Il. 18.254. 3 About or concerning something: τάδʼ ἀ. πονησόμεθα Il. 23.159. Cf. Il. 7.316, Il. 11.776: τὸνδέρον ἀ. θʼ ἕπον Od. 8.61, Od. 19.421. II Prep. (sometimes (without anastrophe) following the case). 1 With dat. a On each side of: ἀ. κῦμα στείρῃ ἴαχεν Il. 1.481, ἀ. ὤμοισιν βάλετο ξίθος (i.e. the belt rested on both shoulders) Il. 2.45, θώρηκας ῥήξειν ἀ. στήθεσσιν (i.e. the belt rested on both shoulders) Il. 2.45, θώρηκας ῥήξειν ἀ. στήθεσσιν (i.e. the two γύαλα) 544, ἀ. ὀχέεσσι βάλε κύκλα Il. 5.722, ἀ. σθοῖς ὀχέεσσιν (app., sprawling over them) Il. 18.231, ἀ. πυρίποδα (astraddle over it) 344, etc.: ἀ. ἑνὶ δούρατι βαῖνεν (bestriding it) Od. 5.371, ἀ. πυπὶ χαλκὸν ἰήνατε Od. 8.426, etc. So with locative: ἱδρώσει τελαμὼν ἀ. στήθεσφιν Il. 2.388. In reference to a shield protecting on both sides (cf. ἀμφίβροτος): δῄουν ἀ. στήθεσσι βοείας Il. 5.452. Cf. Il. 10.149 (across the shoulders), Il. 11.527, Il. 16.108, Il. 17.132, etc. For βαίνειν ἀ. τινι see βαίνω I.6.a, and cf. ἀμφιβαίνω 4. Joined with περί Od. 11.609. b Round, about, round about: τυθωέϊ Il. 2.782, εἰδώλῳ Il. 5.451. Cf. Il. 9.654, Il. 13.496, Il. 14.447, Il. 15.608, etc.: πόλει Od. 6.9, γούνασιν Od. 7.142. Cf. Od. 4.245, Od. 10.262, Od. 11.423, Od. 14.23, etc. So with locative: ἀ. κυνέην κεφαλῆφιν ἔθηκεν Il. 10.257. Cf. Il. 10.261: Od. 16.145. In reference to something transfixing: ἀ. σιδήρῳ Il. 23.30. Cf. Od. 12.395. With notion of protection: ἀ. βόεσσιν Il. 15.587. Cf. Il. 17.369. c About, concerning, for, touching, in the matter of: Ἑλένῃ Il. 3.70. Cf. Il. 3.254, Il. 7.408, Il. 11.672, Il. 13.382, Il. 16.647, etc.: τεύχεσιν ἀ. Ἀχιλῆος Od. 11.546. Cf. Od. 1.48, Od. 4.151, Od. 14.338, Od. 17.555, Od. 22.227, etc. 2 With acc. a On each side of : ἀ. κῆρ Il. 16.481. b Round, about, round about: ἀ. ἅλα(i.e. round the bay) Il. 1.409, ἀ. Αἴαντε (with them, under their leadership) Il. 6.436, τὴν ἑτέρην πόλιν ἀ. Il. 18.509. Cf. Il. 2.417, Il. 3.231, Il. 5.314, Il. 13.335, Il. 16.290, Il. 17.290, Il. 22.473, etc.: Ἰαρδάνου ἀ. ῥέεθρα Od. 3.292. Cf. Od. 3.163, Od. 8.502, Od. 11.419, Od. 17.65, Od. 22.281, Od. 24.37, etc. Joined with περί Il. 2.305, Il. 17.760.–οἱ ἀ. τινα, a person and those with him, a group of which the person named is the chief: οἱ δʼ ἀ. Ἀτρεΐωνα ἠγερέθοντο Il. 23.233. With several persons named Il. 3.146. Sim.: οὓς ἑτάρους στέλλοντʼ ἀ. Πελάγοντα Ἀλάστορά τε . . . Il. 4.295 (where P. etc. are included in ὲτάρους). c About, concerning: ἀ. ἔκαστα Od. 19.46.–(/b>3) With genit., about, concerning: μάχεσθον πίδακος ἀ. Il. 16.825. Cf. Od. 8.267.

αμφιαλοσ.g: -ον [ἀμφι- 3 + ἅλς1.] Sea-girt. Epithet of Ithaca Od. 1.386, 395, 401, Od. 2.293, Od. 8.252.

αμφιβασισ.g: ἡ [ἀμφιβαίνω.] Defence of a fallen body (cf. ἀμφιβαίνω 4): Τρώων (by the . . .) Il. 5.623.

αμφιβροτοσ.g: -η, -ον [ἀμφι- 1 + βροτός.] Protecting on both sides (as well as in front). Epithet of shields Il. 2.389, Il. 11.32, Il. 12.402, Il. 20.281.

αμφιγυηεισ.g: [prob. ἀμφι- 2 + γυ-, to bend, as in γύαλον, γυρός.] Thus, having a crooked limb on each side. Epithet or a name of Hephaestus Il. 1.607, Il. 14.239, Il. 18.383, 393 = 462, 587, 590, 614: Od. 8.300, 349, 357.

αμφιγυοσ.g: [prob. as ἀμφιγυήεις.] Thus, of spears, (having a head) curved on each side, i.e. leafshaped; or perh., bending to either side, elastic Il. 13.147 = Il. 15.278 = Il. 17.731, Il. 14.26 = Il. 16.637, Il. 15.386, 712: Od. 16.474, Od. 24.527.

αμφιδασυσ.g: -εια [ἀμφι- 3 + δασύς.] Covered with hair: αἰγίδα Il. 15.309.

αμφιδρυφησ.g: [ἀμφι- 1 + δρυθ-, δρύπτω.] Having both cheeks torn in mourning: ἄλοχος Il. 2.700.

αμφιδρυφοσ.g: -ον [as ἀμφιδρυφής.] Both torn in mourning: παρειαί Il. 11.393.

αμφιδυμοσ.g: [ἀμφι- 2 + -δυμος as in δίδυμος.] Twofold, double: λιμένες Od. 4.847.

αμφιελισσα.g: -ης [ἀμφι- 1 + (V) ἑλίσσω.] Epithet of ships, wheeling both ways; hence, easily directed, handy Il. 2.165 = 181, Il. 9.683, Il. 13.174 = Il. 15.549, Il. 17.612, Il. 18.260: Od. 3.162, Od. 6.264, Od. 7.9, 252, Od. 9.64, Od. 10.91, 156 = Od. 12.368, Od. 14.258 = Od. 17.427, Od. 15.283, Od. 8.390.

αμφιεπω.g: [ἀμφι- 3, ἀμφι- 4 + (σ)έπω1.] With elision of the ι (on the loss of the σ) 3 sing. impf. ἄμφεπε Il. 17.124, Il. 18.348: Od. 8.437. 3 pl. -ον Il. 18.559, Il. 23.167, Il. 24.622. 1 To handle, attend to, do what is needful to: ἵππους Il. 19.392. Cf. Il. 5.667, Il. 18.559, Il. 23.167, Il. 24.622. 2 To marshal, draw up in order Il. 2.525. 3 To manage, conduct: τάφον Il. 24.804. 4 In sinister sense, to employ oneself about for evil, work for the destruction of, [Τρῶας] Od. 3.118. 5 Of fire, to bring itself to bear upon, lap round: πρύμνην Il. 16.124. Cf. Il. 18.348: = Od. 8.437.

αμφιζανω.g: [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] To settle about, be deposited upon. With dat. Of ashes: χιτῶνι Il. 18.25.

αμφιθαλησ.g: [ἀμφι- 2 + θάλλω.] Absol., one who has both parents alive Il. 22.496.

αμφιθετοσ.g: -ον [ἀμφι- 2 + θε-, τίθημι.] Two-handled: φιάλην Il. 23.270, φιάλη 616.

αμφιθεω.g: [ἀμφι- 3.] To run about or round. With acc., [πόριες] ἀμφιθέουσι μητέρας Od. 10.413.

αμφικαλυπτω.g: [ἀμφι- 1, ἀμφι- 3.] Fut. ἀμφικαλύψω Il. 14.343. Infin. -ειν Od. 8.569, Od. 13.177. 3 sing. aor. ἀμφεκάλυψε Il. 3.442, Il. 5.68, Il. 8.331, Il. 16.350, etc.: Od. 4.180, 618, Od. 15.118. 3 sing. subj. ἀμφικαλύψῃ Od. 8.511, Od. 13.183, Od. 20.86. Pple. ἀμφικαλύψας Od. 5.493, Od. 14.349, Od. 23.17. Infin. ἀμφικαλύψαι Od. 13.152, 158. 1 To cover both of one's . . . (cf. ἀμφί I.1 b ). Of sleep: βλέθαρʼ ἀμφικαλύψας Od. 5.493. Cf. Od. 20.86, Od. 23.17. To cover completely a double (organ) (cf. ἀμφί I 1.b): ἔρως φρένας ἀμφεκάλυψεν Il. 3.442, Il. 14.294. 2 To cover up all round, enfold, conceal, contain Il. 2.262, Il. 23.91. Of a city, to receive within its walls Od. 8.511. Of a house, to receive as a guest Od. 4.618 = Od. 15.118. Fig. of death or fate Il. 5.68, Il. 12.116, Il. 16.350, Il. 20.417: Od. 4.180. 3 To put round, cover or protect with. With dat. of what is covered or protected: σἀκος οἱ Il. 8.331 = Il. 13.420. Cf. Il. 14.343: Od. 14.349. Sim., to put round (something) so as to isolate (it): ὄρος πόλει Od. 8.569, Od. 13.152, 158, 177, 183.

αμφικομοσ.g: [ἀμφι- 3 + κόμη.] With foliage all round, thick-leafed: θάμνῳ Il. 17.677.

αμφικυπελλοσ.g: [ἀμφι- 2 + (perh.) *κυπέλη, handle, conn. with κώπη.] Two-handled: δέπας Il. 1.584, Il. 6.220, Il. 9.656, Il. 23.219, 656, 663, 667, 699: Od. 3.63, Od. 8.89, Od. 13.57, Od. 15.102, 120, Od. 22.86, δέπα Od. 20.153.

αμφιλαχαινω.g: [ἀμφι- 3 + λαχαίνω, to dig.] To dig round about. With acc.: θυτόν Od. 24.242.

αμφιλυκη.g: [ἀμφι- 1 (giving the notion of hesitation between two sides, hence of doubtfulness) + *λύκη = L. lux.] ἀ. νύξ, the(morning) twilight Il. 7.433.

αμφιμαχομαι.g: [ἀμφι- 3, ἀμφι- 4.] 1 With acc., in local sense, to fight round or about: Ἴλιον Il. 6.461. Cf. Il. 9.412, Il. 16.73, Il. 18.208. 2 With genit., to fight for the possession of: τείχεος Il. 15.391. Cf. Il. 16.496 = 533, Il. 18.20.

αμφινεμω.g: [ἀμφι- 3.] In mid., to have one's lot, dwell, round or about. With acc. With place-names Il. 2.521, 574, 585, 634, 649, 655, 835, 853, Il. 18.186: Od. 19.132.

αμφιπελω.g: [ἀμφι- 3.] Of sound, to come round (hearers). With dat. In mid.: ἀοιδὴ ἀκουόντεσσιν Od. 1.352.

αμφιπενομαι.g: [ἀμφι- 4.] To busy oneself about, attend to Il. 13.656, Il. 19.278. To attend upon Od. 15.467. To treat surgically Il. 4.220, Il. 16.28: Od. 19.455. In sinister sense: Ἀστεροπαῖον ἐγχέλυες ἀμφεπένοντο (made a meal of him) Il. 21.203. Cf. Il. 23.184.

αμφιπεριστεφω.g: [ἀμφι- 3 + περι- 1.] To put round. With dat. Fig., in pass., to be put round as a crown, adorn: οὔ οἱ χάρις ἀμφιπεριστέθεται ἐπέεσσιν Od. 8.175.

αμφιπεριστρωφαω.g: [ἀμφι- 3 + περι- 2.] To turn about in all directions: ἵππους Il. 8.348.

αμφιπολευω.g: [ἀμφίπολος.] To busy oneself about, take care of, tend: ἐμὸν βίον Od. 18.254 = Od. 19.127, ὄρχατον Od. 24.244, 257. In sinister sense: ἔδοσαν ἐρινύσιν ἀμφιπολεύειν (i.e. handed them over to their tender mercies) Od. 20.78.

αμφιπολοσ.g: -ου, ἡ [ἀμφι- 4 + -πολος, conn. with πολεύω.] A handmaid, a female attendant or servant, hardly to be distinguished from δμῳή. (The words are sometimes used indifferently; cf. Od. 6.52 with 307, and 84 with 99. But in Od. 22.483, 484 ἀμφίπολοι seem to be personal attendants and δμῳαί the other servants.) Il. 3.143, 422, Il. 6.286, 324, 372, 399, 491, 499, Il. 18.417 (i.e. representations), Il. 22.442, 461, Il. 24.304: Od. 1.136, Od. 6.18, Od. 7.232, Od. 18.198, Od. 19.90, Od. 23.227, etc. Of Circe's servants Od. 10.348, 368, Od. 12.18. With γυνή. See γυνή 3. With word indicating the servant's country of origin: σικελή Od. 24.366. Her office: ταμίην Il. 24.302: Od. 16.152.

αμφιπονεομαι.g: [ἀμφι- 4.] To busy oneself about, attend to: τάθον Od. 20.307. To do the offices of a second to: εὐρύαλον Il. 23.681.

αμφιποταομαι.g: [ἀμφι- 3.] To fly round and round Il. 2.315.

αμφιρυτοσ.g: -η [ἀμφι- 3 + ῥυ-, ῥέω.] Flowed round (by the sea), sea-girt Od. 1.50, 198, Od. 11.325, Od. 12.283.

αμφισ.g: [ἀμφί.] I Adv. 1 On both sides: ᾧ ῥόπαλʼ ἀ. ἐάγῃ (i.e. across his back) Il. 11.559, δούρασιν ἀ. [βάλεν] (with spears from both hands, with both spears at once) Il. 21.162. 2 A part, asunder: ἀ. φράζονται (have different views) Il. 2.13 = 30 = 67, ἔχουσα ἀ. (one in each scale) Il. 12.434, τόξων ἀϊκὰς ἀ. μένον (at a safe distance) Il. 15.709, ἀ. ἀρωγοί (partisans, some of one, some of the other) Il. 18.502, ἀ. ἀριζήλω (standing out from the others) 519, ἀ. ἄλλʼ ἀποδάσσεσθαι (in addition) Il. 22.117, ἀ. ὁδοῦ Il. 23.393 (see ὁδός 1). Cf. Il. 13.345, 706: ζυγὸν ἀ. ἔχοντες (supporting it at either end) Od. 3.486 = Od. 15.184, τιμὴν ἀ. ἄγοντες (in addition) Od. 22.57. Cf. Od. 1.54. 3 Absent: ἀ. ἐόντα Od. 24.218. Sim. of separation from a person Od. 19.221. 4 Between: ὀλίγη ἦν ἀ. ἄρουρα (between the heaps or rows) Il. 3.115. 5 Round, about: τάθρος ἀ. ἐοῦσα (surrounding) Il. 7.342, τάρταρος ἀ. [ἐστιν] Il. 8.481. Cf. Il. 9.464, Il. 14.123, Il. 23.330, Il. 24.488: Od. 8.340, 476. II Prep. 1 With genit. a Apart from, at a distance from: διός Il. 8.444. Cf. Od. 14.352, Od. 16.267. b About, concerning: ἅρματος ἀ. ἰδών (seeing to it) Il. 2.384. 2 With dat., round, about: ἄξονι Il. 5.723. 3 With acc. a On each side of: δύο δʼ ἀ. ἕκαστον [δίθρον] (one on each side of each) Il. 11.748. b Round, about: ἕκαστον Il. 11.634. Cf. Il. 14.274, Il. 15.225: Od. 6.266, Od. 7.4, Od. 9.399.

αμφιστρεφησ.g: [app. ἀμφι- 3 + στρέφω.] Thus, twisted about: κεφαλαὶ τρεῖς δράκοντος ἀμφιστρεφέες Il. 11.40 (i.e. two twisted about the third).

αμφιτρομεω.g: [ἀμφι- 4.] To tremble for. With genit.: τοῦ Od. 4.820.

αμφιφαλοσ.g: -ον [ἀμφι- 2 + θάλος.] With two θάλοι: κυνέην Il. 5.743 = Il. 11.41.

αμφιφορευσ.g: -ῆος, ὁ [ἀμφι- 2 + θορ-, θέρω.] A two-handled jar Il. 23.92, 170: Od. 2.290, 349, 379, Od. 9.164, 204, Od. 13.105 (of natural formations in a cave), Od. 24.74.

αμφιχεω.g: [ἀμφι- 3.] 3 sing. aor. pass. ἀμφέχυτο Il. 2.41. ἀμφθεχύθη Od. 4.716. Pple. ἀμφιχυθείς Il. 14.253, Il. 23.63: Od. 16.214. Infin. ἀμφιχυθῆναι Il. 23.764. 1 To pour or shed round or about. Of dust: πάρος κόνιν ἀμφιχυθῆναι (had settled down again) Il. 23.764. 2 Fig., in pass., of sound, to come round. With acc.: ἀμφέχυτό μιν ὀμφή Il. 2.41. Of sleep, to be shed round one, come upon one Il. 14.253 Il. 23.63. Of grief, to come upon. With acc.: τὴν ἄχος ἀμφεχύθη Od. 4.716. So of a bodily action, to embrace (a person): ἀμφιχυθεὶς πατέρα Od. 16.214. Cf. Od. 22.498.

αμφιχυτοσ.g: [ἀμφιχέω.] Poured round or about; hence of heaped-up earth: τεῖχος Il. 20.145.

αμφοτεροσ.g: -η, -ον [ἄμφω.] 1 Both. a Of two persons, etc. In dual or (more freq.) in pl. α Absol.: ἐξαίνυτο θυμὸν ἀμφοτέρω Il. 5.156. Cf. Il. 3.208, Il. 4.38, Il. 5.261, Il. 7.3, etc.: ἀμφοτέρους ἱέρευσεν Od. 14.74. Cf. Od. 3.37, Od. 11.212, Od. 18.17, Od. 8.214, etc. β With sb. or pron.: ἀμφοτέρω σθῶϊ Il. 7.280, ἐπʼ ἀμφοτέρους πόδας (one after the other) Il. 13.281. Cf. Il. 4.521, Il. 5.163, Il. 8.115, Il. 12.382, etc.: ἀμφοτέρῃσιν χερσίν Od. 4.116. Cf. Od. 3.136, Od. 4.282, Od. 5.414, Od. 12.239, etc. With sb. to be supplied: ἀμφοτέρῃσι [χερσίν], with both hands Il. 5.416: Od. 10.264, Od. 11.594, Od. 17.356, Od. 18.28. b In pl. of two groups of persons. α Absol.: ἀμφοτέρων βέλεα Il. 8.67. Cf. Il. 3.416, Il. 4.16, Il. 6.120, Il. 13.303, etc.: φιλότητα μετʼ ἀμφοτέροισιν Od. 24.476. Cf. Od. 10.204, Od. 24.546. β With pron.: τοὺς ἀμφοτέρους Il. 20.54. 2 In neut. ἀμφότερον as adv., both. Followed by . . . τε . . . τε Il. 3.179, Il. 4.145. By . . . τε καὶ . . . Il. 4.60 = Il. 18.365, Il. 13.166. By . . . τε . . . δὲ . . . Il. 7.418. By καὶ Od. 14.505. By . . . τε καὶ . . . καὶ . . . Od. 15.78.

αμφοτερωθεν.g: [ἀμφότερος + -θεν 1.] 1 From both sides: ὦρτʼ ἀϋτὴ ἀ. Il. 15.313. Cf. Il. 12.431. Of plainting strands of a rope, across and across Od. 10.167. 2 On both sides, on either side: πλῆμναί εἰσιν ἀ. Il. 5.726. Cf. Il. 12.55, Il. 16.563, Il. 17.440, Il. 20.170, Il. 23.628: Od. 22.404. On both edges: ἀ. ἀκαχμένον Od. 5.235, Od. 22.80. At both ends: ἅψας ἀ. Od. 8.408. Of stating alternatives: ἐρέω ἀ. Od. 12.58. 3 In both directions: θόως γένετʼ ἀ. Il. 15.669. With περί, app., in both directions so as to meet: περὶ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται ἀ. Od. 7.113. Cf. Od. 10.88.

αμφοτερωσε.g: [ἀμφότερος + -σε.] In both directions: γεγωνέμεν ἀ. Il. 8.223 = Il. 11.6, ἀ. λίθοι πωτῶντο Il. 12.287.

αμφουδισ.g: [prob. ἀμφι- 3 + an unknown element + advbl. -δις.] App., by the middle: ἀ. ἀείρας Od. 17.237.

αμφω.g: Only in nom. and acc. of same form. Both. Constructed with dual or pl. 1 Of two persons, etc. a Absol.: ἀ. θιλέουσα Il. 1.196. Cf. Il. 1.259, Il. 2.767, Il. 3.148, Il. 5.153, etc.: ἀ. ἱέσθην Od. 3.344. Cf. Od. 8.316, Od. 10.138, Od. 12.424, Od. 13.296, Od. 15.366, Od. 18.65, 372. b With sb. or pron.: ἀ. χεῖρε Il. 4.523. Cf. Il. 5.258, Il. 6.19, Il. 7.255, Il. 11.782, etc.: τοὺς ἀ. Od. 11.301. Cf. Od. 5.453, Od. 8.135, Od. 16.15, Od. 18.89, etc. 2 Of two groups of persons: ἀριθμηθήμεναι ἀ. Il. 2.124.

αμφωτοσ.g: [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 2 + ὠτ-, οὖς.] Having two ears (for handles) : ἄλεισον Od. 22.10.

αμωμητοσ.g: [ἀ-1 + μωμάομαι.] Not to be blamed; hence, unerring (in counsel): πουλυδάμαντος Il. 12.109.

αν1..g: Conditional or limiting particle. (Cf. κεν.) For the uses with subj., opt. and fut., aor. and impf. indic. in protasis and apodosis see 6. 1 With subj.: τάχʼ ἂν θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ Il. 1.205. Cf. Il. 18.192, Il. 22.505: ἐγὼ ἂν ξεῖνος ἔω Od. 9.17. Cf. Od. 4.240, Od. 11.328, 517, Od. 12.81. In Il. 22.50 (ἀπολυσόμεθα) : Od. 4.240, Od. 11.328, 517 (μυθήσομαι), Od. 6.221 (λοέσσομαι) may be aor. subj. or fut. indic. 2 With opt. in potential or fut. sense: τῶν οὐκ ἄν τι θέροις Il. 1.301. Cf. Il. 2.250 (conveying an order), Il. 3.52 (will you not . . .?), 66, Il. 5.32, 362, Il. 6.141, Il. 9.77, Il. 10.204, Il. 13.741, Il. 14.58, Il. 22.108, Il. 24.437, etc.: πῶς ἂν Ὀδυσῆος λαθοίμην; Od. 1.65. Cf. Od. 3.232, Od. 4.78, Od. 6.57, 300, Od. 10.573, Od. 20.135 (do not . . .), Od. 22.325, etc. 3 In potential sense in reference to the past in suppositions contrary to fact. a With impf. or aor. indic.: ἦ τʼ ἂν κέρδιον ἦεν Il. 5.201 = Il. 22.103, οὐκ ἂν θυμὸν ὤρινεν Il. 19.271. Cf. Il. 8.455, Il. 13.676, Il. 16.638: οὐκ ἂν τόσσʼ ἀγόρευες (would not have . . .) Od. 2.184. Cf. Od. 9.211, 228, 334. b With pres. or aor. opt.: ἦ ἄν ὕστατα λωβήσαιο Il. 1.232 = Il. 2.242. Cf. Il. 1.271, Il. 4.223, Il. 5.85 Il. 13.127: οὐκ ἄν ὀχλίσσειαν Od. 9.241. 4 With infin. in indirect discourse: καὶ δʼ ἂν τοῖς ἄλλοισιν ἔθη παραμυθήσασθαι Il. 9.684. 5 Joined with κεν. See κεν 5. 6 For uses in protasis with εἰ and in the corresponding relative sentences see Table at end II.B.a 3 subj., (D) (7) subj., (23) opt., III.B.a 3 subj., (D) (11) fut., (34) (35) (36) (37) (38) (43) (44) subj., (49) (65) opt. For uses in apodosis see II.C.a 3 aor. or impf. indic., (6) opt., c.2 opt., (D) (6) opt., (23) fut., (30) opt., (52) subj., (57) (63) opt. For ὅτʼ ἄν (not in protasis) see ὅτε 1.a.γ, b.α b.δ b.ε, 4. For ὄφρʼ ἅν (not in protasis) see ὄφρα 1.b, ὄφρα 1.c, 5.a b . For ὡς ἄν (not in protasis) see ὡς 7.a, b.β, 8.α 8.γ, b.γ.

ανα.g: Also in form ἄν and in assimilated form ἄμ. I Adv. 1 Up, upwards, in an upward direction, on to something: ἂν Χρυσηΐδα βήσομεν (put her on board) Il. 1.143, ἀνὰ δʼ ἔστη Il. 2.100, ἂν δʼ ἔβη (mounted) Il. 3.261, ἀνʼ ἔντεα λέγοντες (gathering them up) Il. 11.755. Cf. Il. 1.310, Il. 3.268, Il. 5.798, Il. 17.541, Il. 21.361, Il. 22.77, etc.: ἂν δʼ αὐτοὶ βάντες (going on board) Od. 2.419 = Od. 4.579. Cf. Od. 6.253, Od. 8.3, Od. 9.468 (see νεύω 3), Od. 13.56, Od. 17.262 (see βάλλω II.4), etc. 2 Back, reversal of action: ἀνά τʼ ἔδραμʼ ὀπίσσω Il. 5.599, ἀνὰ δὲ σχέο Il. 7.110 (see ἔχω IV.1.b): ἀνὰ πρυμνήσια λῦσαι Od. 9.178 = 562 = Od. 11.637 = Od. 12.145 = Od. 15.548. 3 Indicating extension or diffusion: ἀνʼ ἱστία πέτασσαν Il. 1.480, μέλανες ἀνὰ βότρυες ἦσαν Il. 18.562: ἀνὰ κρητῆρα κέρασσεν Od. 3.390. Cf. Od. 4.41, 783 = Od. 8.54, Od. 10.506, Od. 24.343. II Prep. 1 With dat., on, upon: ἀνὰ σκήπτρῳ Il. 1.15 = 374. Cf. Il. 14.352, Il. 15.152: ἂμ πέτρῃσιν Od. 5.156. Cf. Od. 11.128 = Od. 23.128 = Od. 23.275, Od. 24.8. In pregnant sense: ἅρματʼ ἂμ βωμοῖσι τίθει Il. 8.441. Cf. Il. 18.177. 2 With acc. a On to, on, upon: θῆκεν ἀνὰ μυρίκην Il. 10.466. Cf. Il. 18.278: ἂν δὲ βήσετο δίφρον Od. 3.481. Cf. Od. 3.492 = Od. 15.145 = 190, Od. 22.176, 193, 239. b Through, throughout, along, over, among, in, on: ἀνὰ στρατόν Il. 1.10, ἂμ πεδίον Il. 5.87. Cf. Il. 1.53, Il. 4.251, Il. 5.74, Il. 9.383, Il. 10.339, Il. 13.308, Il. 16.349, Il. 22.452 (in . . .), etc.: ἂν στόμα Od. 5.456, ἀνʼ ὀρσοθύρην Od. 22.132. Cf. Od. 2.430, Od. 7.72, Od. 10.251, Od. 18.246, Od. 22.18, Od. 24.318, etc. In reference to the mouth as the organ of speech: βασιλῆας ἀνὰ στόμʼ ἔχων (having them passing through the mouth, i.e. talking freely of them) Il. 2.250. In reference to immaterial things: ἀνὰ θυμόν (in his mind) Il. 2.36, ἀνʼ ἰθύν Il. 21.303 (see ἰθύς2 2), etc. Cf. Od. 2.116, Od. 4.638, Od. 8.377 (see ἰθύς2 1), etc. In reference to night as a space of darkness: ἀνὰ νύκτα Il. 14.80. Indicating diffusion: ἀνὰ εἴκοσι μέτρα Od. 9.209. In reference to position: ἀνὰ πρόθυρον τετραμμένος (i.e. with his feet pointing outwards through the doorway) Il. 19.212. 3 With genit., on to, upon: ἂν δὲ νηὸς βαῖνεν (went on board) Od. 2.416. Cf. Od. 9.177, Od. 15.284.

ανα1.g: [ἀνά with anastrophe.] Up ! get up ! rouse yourself ! to work ! ἀλλʼ ἄνα Il. 6.331, Il. 9.247, Il. 18.178: Od. 18.13.

αναβαινω.g: [ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 2 5.] A Contr. 1 pl. subj. ἀμβαίνωμεν Od. 15.219. Contr. infin. ἀμβαίνειν Od. 9.178, Od. 11.637, etc. 3 sing. aor. ἀνέβη Il. 1.497. 3 sing subj. ἀναβῇ Od. 2.358. 3 sing. opt. ἀναβαίη Od. 22.132. Contr. ἀμβαίη Od. 12.77. Pple. ἀναβάς, -άντος Il. 1.312, 611, Il. 14.287, Il. 16.184, etc.: Od. 3.157, Od. 5.470, Od. 14.353, Od. 15.474, etc. Fem. ἀναβᾶσα Od. 1.362, Od. 17.49, Od. 22.428, etc. Infin. ἀναβήμεναι Od. 1.210. 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνεβήσετο Od. 23.1. B Aor. pple. pl. mid. ἀναβησάμενοι Od. 15.475. I Intrans. in all forms except (B). 1 To go up, ascend, mount: ἐς λέχος Il. 1.611. Cf. Il. 14.287, Il. 16.184, 657, Il. 22.399: εἰς ὑπερῷα Od. 1.362 = Od. 19.602 = Od. 21.356, Od. 2.358, Od. 4.751 = Od. 17.49 = Od. 23.364, Od. 4.760, Od. 23.1. Cf. Od. 3.483, Od. 5.470, Od. 14.353. Absol. Od. 12.77. In reference to leaving a room: ἀνʼ ὀρσοθύρην Od. 22.132, ἀνέβαινεν ἐς θαλάμους (left the μέγαρον and took his way to . . .) Od. 22.142. Of a voyage from Ithaca to Troy Od. 1.210. 2 To go up to, ascend to. With acc.: οὐρανόν Il. 1.497. Cf. Od. 18.302, Od. 19.600, Od. 22.428. 3 To go on board a ship, embark: ἀναβάντες ἐπέπλεον ὑγρὰ κέλευθα Il. 1.312: ἀναβάντες ἐλαύνομεν Od. 3.157. Cf. Od. 4.473, 842, Od. 9.178 = 562 = Od. 11.637 = Od. 12.145 = Od. 15.548, Od. 12.293, 401, Od. 13.285, Od. 14.252, Od. 15.209, 219, 474. 4 Of reputation, to be spread abroad among. With acc.: φάτις ἀνθρώπους ἀναβαίνει Od. 6.29. II Trans. in form (B), to cause to go on board a ship or embark: νὼ ἀναβησάμενοι Od. 15.475.

αναβαλλω.g: [ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3.] Contr. 1 pl. subj. mid. ἀμβαλλώμεθα Il. 2.436. 1 To put off, delay: ἄεθλον Od. 19.584. In mid.: ἔργον Il. 2.436. 2 In mid., to strike up, begin (to sing) (cf. βάλλω II.4 and ἀμβλήδην): ἀνεβάλλετʼ ἀείδειν Od. 1.155, Od. 8.266.

αναβλησισ.g: ἡ [ἀναβάλλω.] 1 Delay: λύσιος νεκροῖο (in . . .) Il. 24.655. 2 Respite: κακοῦ (from . . .) Il. 2.380.

αναγκαιη.g: -ης, ἡ. Instrumental ἀναγκαίηφι Il. 20.143. = ἀνάγκη Il. 6.85: Od. 19.73. In dat. ἀναγκαίῃ, of necessity Il. 4.300. In instrumental, by the application of force or strength: δαμέντας Il. 20.143.

αναγκαιοσ.g: -η, -ον [ἀνάγκη.] 1 Compelled, acting under compulsion: πολεμισταί Od. 24.499. Sim. of slaves Od. 24.210. 2 Imposing compulsion: ἦμαρ ἀναγκαῖον (see ἦμαρ 4.b) Il. 16.836, μύθῳ Od. 17.399 = Od. 20.344.–χρειοῖ ἀναγκαίῃ, by compelling necessity, under the compulsion of necessity Il. 8.57.

αναγκη.g: -ης, ἡ. 1 Necessity, compulsion: ἐπικείσετʼ ἀ. Il. 6.458. Cf. Il. 5.633, Il. 10.418, Il. 20.251, Il. 24.667: Od. 10.273.–ὑπʼ ἀνάγκης, under compulsion Od. 2.110 = Od. 24.146, Od. 19.156. 2 In dat. ἀνάγκῃ. a By or under compulsion or constraint: ἀ. οὔ μιν ἄξω Il. 9.429. Cf. Il. 9.692, Il. 15.199: ὃς ἤειδεν ἀ. Od. 1.154. Cf. Od. 4.557, Od. 5.154, Od. 7.217, Od. 9.98, Od. 14.27, etc. b Under compulsion of circumstances, of necessity, perforce: φεύγοντας Il. 11.150. Cf. Il. 12.178, Il. 14.128, Il. 15.133, etc.: ἄγρην ἐφέπεσκον Od. 12.330. Cf. Od. 13.307, Od. 15.311.

αναγω.g: [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] 1 pl. fut. ἀνάξομεν Od. 18.115. Aor. ἀνήγαγον Il. 15.29. 3 sing. -ε Il. 6.292, Il. 9.338: Od. 3.272, Od. 4.534. 1 To cause to go or take inland Od. 14.272 = Od. 17.441. 2 Of bringing to Troy Il. 3.48, Il. 6.292, Il. 9.338, Il. 13.627. To Argos Il. 15.29. Of taking from Ithaca to the mainland Od. 18.115. 3 Of bringing gifts to temples Il. 8.203. 4 Of conducting to a house: ὅνδε δόμονδε Od. 3.272. Without complementary words Od. 4.534. 5 To bring up to the mark in a contest Od. 18.89. 6 In mid., to put to sea, sail Il. 1.478: Od. 19.202.

αναδεσμη.g: -ης, ἡ [ἀνα- 6 + δεσ-, δέω.] A woman's head-dress, app. in the form of a plaited band Il. 22.469.

αναεδνοσ.g: ἡ [app. for ἀνέϝεδνος fr. ἀν- 1 + ἔϝεδνα. See ἕδνα, ἔεδνα.] Without bride-price Il. 9.146, 288, Il. 13.366.

αναειρω.g: [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνάειρε Il. 23.614, 725, 729, 778. Infin. ἀναεῖραι Od. 8.298. 1 To lift up, raise Od. 8.298. Of a wrestler hoisting his adversary Il. 23.724, 725, 729. 2 To take up, pick up Il. 23.614, 778.

αναθημα.g: -ατος, τό [ἀνατίθημι.] An accompaniment or accessory: δαιτός Od. 1.152, Od. 21.430.
